lessons.title: Exercise 4.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The nth term of an A.P. is aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d; for 2, 5, 8, ... the 15th term is 44.
  • If a₁ = 8 and a₂₁ = 108, then d = 5 and the 7th term is 38.
  • The A.P. 6, 9, 12, ..., 78 has 25 terms.
  • aₙ = 2n + 7 gives an A.P. with common difference 2 and 7th term 21.
  • log a, log(ab), log(ab²), ... is an A.P. with common difference log b and nth term log(abⁿ⁻¹).
  • The arithmetic mean of a and b is A = (a + b)/(2); the A.M. of 12 and 18 is 15 and of (1)/(3) and (1)/(4) is (7)/(24).
  • For n arithmetic means between a and b, d = (b - a)/(n + 1); four means between 17 and 32 are 20, 23, 26, 29.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1. Find the 15th term of the arithmetic sequence 2, 5, 8, ....

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = 2.
d = 5 - 2 = 3.
n = 15.
a₁₅ = 2 + (15 - 1)(3)
a₁₅ = 2 + (14)(3)
a₁₅ = 2 + 42
a₁₅ = 44
Answer: 44

Q: Q2. The 1st term of an arithmetic sequence is 8 and the 21st term is 108. Find the 7th term.

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = 8 and a₂₁ = 108.
a₂₁ = 8 + (21 - 1)d = 108
8 + 20d = 108
20d = 108 - 8 = 100
d = (100)/(20) = 5
a₇ = 8 + (7 - 1)(5)
a₇ = 8 + (6)(5)
a₇ = 8 + 30
a₇ = 38
Answer: 38

Q: Q3. Find the number of terms in the arithmetic progression 6, 9, 12, ....., 78.

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = 6, d = 9 - 6 = 3 and aₙ = 78.
78 = 6 + (n - 1)(3)
78 - 6 = (n - 1)(3)
72 = (n - 1)(3)
n - 1 = (72)/(3) = 24
n = 24 + 1 = 25
Answer: 25 terms
Note: The book's printed answer (26) is incorrect; the correct answer is 25.

Q: Q4. The nth term of a sequence is given by aₙ = 2n + 7. Show that it is an A.P. Also, find its 7th term.

Ans: Formula: a sequence is an A.P. if aₙ₊₁ - aₙ is constant
Given: aₙ = 2n + 7
Then aₙ₊₁ = 2(n + 1) + 7
= 2n + 2 + 7
= 2n + 9
aₙ₊₁ - aₙ = (2n + 9) - (2n + 7)
= 2
The difference is constant (= 2), so the sequence is an A.P. Hence proved.
a₇ = 2(7) + 7
a₇ = 14 + 7 = 21
Answer: The sequence is an A.P. with common difference 2, and its 7th term is 21

Q: Q5. Show that the sequence log a, log(ab), log(ab²), log(ab³), ......... is an A.P. Find its nth term.

Ans: Given: the sequence log a, log(ab), log(ab²), log(ab³), ...
To Prove: the sequence is an A.P., and its nth term is log(abⁿ⁻¹)
log(ab) - log a = log((ab)/(a)) = log b
log(ab²) - log(ab) = log((ab²)/(ab)) = log b
log(ab³) - log(ab²) = log((ab³)/(ab²)) = log b
Every difference is the same constant log b.
So the sequence is an A.P. with a₁ = log a and d = log b. Hence proved.
Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
aₙ = log a + (n - 1) log b
aₙ = log a + log bⁿ⁻¹
aₙ = log(abⁿ⁻¹)
Answer: The sequence is an A.P. and its nth term is log(abⁿ⁻¹)

Q: Q6. Find the value of 'k' if 2k + 7, 6k - 2, 8k - 4 are in A.P. Also find the sequence.

Ans: Formula: if x, y, z are in A.P. then y - x = z - y
Here x = 2k + 7, y = 6k - 2, z = 8k - 4.
(6k - 2) - (2k + 7) = (8k - 4) - (6k - 2)
4k - 9 = 2k - 2
4k - 2k = -2 + 9
2k = 7
k = (7)/(2)
First term = 2k + 7 = 2 × (7)/(2) + 7 = 7 + 7 = 14
Second term = 6k - 2 = 6 × (7)/(2) - 2 = 21 - 2 = 19
Third term = 8k - 4 = 8 × (7)/(2) - 4 = 28 - 4 = 24
The common difference is 19 - 14 = 5.
Answer: k = (7)/(2), and the sequence is 14, 19, 24, ...

Q: Q7. If a₆ + a₄ = 6 and a₆ - a₄ = (2)/(3), find the arithmetic sequence.

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
a₆ + a₄ = 6 gives (a₁ + 5d) + (a₁ + 3d) = 6
2a₁ + 8d = 6 ... (i)
a₆ - a₄ = (2)/(3) gives (a₁ + 5d) - (a₁ + 3d) = (2)/(3)
2d = (2)/(3)
d = (1)/(3)
Put d = (1)/(3) in (i): 2a₁ + 8 × (1)/(3) = 6
2a₁ = 6 - (8)/(3) = (10)/(3)
a₁ = (5)/(3)
The terms are a₁ = (5)/(3), a₂ = (5)/(3) + (1)/(3) = 2, a₃ = 2 + (1)/(3) = (7)/(3), ...
Answer: (5)/(3), 2, (7)/(3), ...

Q: Q8. If (b + c - a)/(a), (c + a - b)/(b), (a + b - c)/(c) are in A.P. then prove (1)/(a), (1)/(b), (1)/(c) are in A.P.

Ans: Given: (b + c - a)/(a), (c + a - b)/(b), (a + b - c)/(c) are in A.P.
To Prove: (1)/(a), (1)/(b), (1)/(c) are in A.P.
(b + c - a)/(a) = (a + b + c)/(a) - (2a)/(a)
= (a + b + c)/(a) - 2
Similarly, (c + a - b)/(b) = (a + b + c)/(b) - 2
and (a + b - c)/(c) = (a + b + c)/(c) - 2
Adding 2 to each term of an A.P. keeps it an A.P.
So (a + b + c)/(a), (a + b + c)/(b), (a + b + c)/(c) are in A.P.
Dividing each term by the constant (a + b + c) keeps it an A.P.
So (1)/(a), (1)/(b), (1)/(c) are in A.P.
Hence proved.

Q: Q9. A ball rolling up an incline covered 24m during the first second, 21m during the second, 18m during the third second. Find how many meters it covered in the eighth second?

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
The distances 24, 21, 18, ... form an A.P.
Here a₁ = 24.
d = 21 - 24 = -3.
n = 8.
a₈ = 24 + (8 - 1)(-3)
a₈ = 24 + (7)(-3)
a₈ = 24 - 21
a₈ = 3
Answer: 3 m

Q: Q10. The population of a town is decreasing by 500 inhabitants each year. If its population in 1960 was 20135, what was its population in 1970?

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Take the population in 1960 as the first term: a₁ = 20135.
The population decreases by 500 each year, so d = -500.
From 1960 to 1970 there are 10 steps, so 1970 is the 11th term: n = 11.
a₁₁ = 20135 + (11 - 1)(-500)
a₁₁ = 20135 + (10)(-500)
a₁₁ = 20135 - 5000
a₁₁ = 15135
Answer: 15135

Q: Q11. Ahmad and Akram can climb 1000 feet in the first hour and 100 feet in each succeeding hour. When will they reach the top of a 5400 feet hill?

Ans: Formula: distance climbed in n hours = first hour distance + (n - 1) × distance in each later hour
Distance in the first hour = 1000 feet.
Distance in each succeeding hour = 100 feet.
Total distance to climb = 5400 feet.
1000 + (n - 1)(100) = 5400
(n - 1)(100) = 5400 - 1000 = 4400
n - 1 = (4400)/(100) = 44
n = 44 + 1 = 45
Answer: 45 hours

Q: Q12. A man earned $3500 the first year he worked. If he received a raise of $750 at the end of each year for 20 years, what was his salary during his twenty first year of work?

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = 3500 and d = 750.
The twenty first year is n = 21.
a₂₁ = 3500 + (21 - 1)(750)
a₂₁ = 3500 + (20)(750)
a₂₁ = 3500 + 15000
a₂₁ = 18500
Answer: $18500

Q: Q13(i). Find the arithmetic mean between the given numbers: 12, 18

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2)
Here a = 12 and b = 18.
A = (12 + 18)/(2)
A = (30)/(2)
A = 15
Answer: 15

Q: Q13(ii). Find the arithmetic mean between the given numbers: (1)/(3), (1)/(4)

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2)
Here a = (1)/(3) and b = (1)/(4).
A = (((1)/(3) + (1)/(4)))/(2)
A = (((7)/(12)))/(2)
A = (7)/(24)
Answer: (7)/(24)

Q: Q13(iii). Find the arithmetic mean between the given numbers: -6, -216

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2)
Here a = -6 and b = -216.
A = (-6 + (-216))/(2)
A = (-222)/(2)
A = -111
Answer: -111

Q: Q13(iv). Find the arithmetic mean between the given numbers: (a + b)², (a - b)²

Ans: Formula: A = (x + y)/(2), with x = (a + b)² and y = (a - b)²
A = ((a + b)² + (a - b)²)/(2)
(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²
(a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b²
(a + b)² + (a - b)² = 2a² + 2b²
A = (2a² + 2b²)/(2)
A = a² + b²
Answer: a² + b²

Q: Q14(i). Insert three arithmetic means between 6 and 41.

Ans: Formula: d = (b - a)/(n + 1) for n means between a and b
Here a = 6, b = 41 and n = 3.
d = (41 - 6)/(3 + 1)
d = (35)/(4)
First mean = a + d = 6 + (35)/(4) = (59)/(4) = 14(3)/(4)
Second mean = a + 2d = 6 + 2 × (35)/(4) = (47)/(2) = 23(1)/(2)
Third mean = a + 3d = 6 + 3 × (35)/(4) = (129)/(4) = 32(1)/(4)
Answer: 14(3)/(4), 23(1)/(2), 32(1)/(4)

Q: Q14(ii). Insert four arithmetic means between 17 and 32.

Ans: Formula: d = (b - a)/(n + 1) for n means between a and b
Here a = 17, b = 32 and n = 4.
d = (32 - 17)/(4 + 1)
d = (15)/(5) = 3
First mean = 17 + 3 = 20
Second mean = 17 + 2(3) = 23
Third mean = 17 + 3(3) = 26
Fourth mean = 17 + 4(3) = 29
Answer: 20, 23, 26, 29

Q: Q15. For what value of n, (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) is the arithmetic mean between a and b?

Ans: Formula: the arithmetic mean between a and b is (a + b)/(2)
Set (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) = (a + b)/(2)
Cross-multiplying: 2aⁿ⁺¹ + 2bⁿ⁺¹ = (a + b)(aⁿ + bⁿ)
2aⁿ⁺¹ + 2bⁿ⁺¹ = aⁿ⁺¹ + abⁿ + aⁿb + bⁿ⁺¹
Simplifying: aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹ = abⁿ + aⁿb
aⁿ⁺¹ - aⁿb = abⁿ - bⁿ⁺¹
aⁿ(a - b) = bⁿ(a - b)
Since a ≠ b, divide by (a - b): aⁿ = bⁿ
This holds when n = 0.
Check for n = 0: (a + b)/(a⁰ + b⁰) = (a + b)/(2), which is the arithmetic mean.
Answer: n = 0

Q: Q16. Insert five arithmetic means between 5 and 8 and show that their sum is five times the arithmetic mean between 5 and 8.

Ans: Formula: d = (b - a)/(n + 1) for n means between a and b
Here a = 5, b = 8 and n = 5.
d = (8 - 5)/(5 + 1)
d = (3)/(6) = (1)/(2)
First mean = 5 + (1)/(2) = (11)/(2)
Second mean = 5 + 2 × (1)/(2) = 6
Third mean = 5 + 3 × (1)/(2) = (13)/(2)
Fourth mean = 5 + 4 × (1)/(2) = 7
Fifth mean = 5 + 5 × (1)/(2) = (15)/(2)
Sum of the means = (11)/(2) + 6 + (13)/(2) + 7 + (15)/(2)
= (11 + 12 + 13 + 14 + 15)/(2) = (65)/(2)
Arithmetic mean between 5 and 8 = (5 + 8)/(2) = (13)/(2)
Five times the arithmetic mean = 5 × (13)/(2) = (65)/(2)
The two values are equal. Hence proved.
Answer: The five means are (11)/(2), 6, (13)/(2), 7, (15)/(2), and their sum is five times the arithmetic mean between 5 and 8

Q: Q17. There are n arithmetic means between 5 and 32 such that the ratio of the 3rd and 7th means is 7:13, find the value of n.

Ans: Formula: for n means between a and b, d = (b - a)/(n + 1) and the kth mean is a + kd
Here a = 5 and b = 32, so d = (32 - 5)/(n + 1) = (27)/(n + 1).
3rd mean = 5 + 3d
7th mean = 5 + 7d
Given ratio: (5 + 3d)/(5 + 7d) = (7)/(13)
Cross-multiplying: 13(5 + 3d) = 7(5 + 7d)
65 + 39d = 35 + 49d
65 - 35 = 49d - 39d
30 = 10d
d = 3
So (27)/(n + 1) = 3
n + 1 = (27)/(3) = 9
n = 8
Answer: n = 8

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d] = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) for an arithmetic series.
  • For 9, 7, 5, 3, ... the 20th term is -29 and S₂₀ = -200.
  • With a₁ = 2, n = 17, d = 3: a₁₇ = 50 and S₁₇ = 442.
  • The sum of all numbers divisible by 5 from 25 through 350 is 12375 (66 terms).
  • Three numbers in A.P. with sum 36 and sum of cubes 6336 are 8, 12, 16.
  • The sum of all multiples of 9 between 300 and 700 is 21978 (44 terms).
  • A theatre with 40 rows, 20 seats in row 1 increasing by 3 per row, has 3140 seats.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the indicated term and the sum of the indicated number of terms in the arithmetic sequence: 9, 7, 5, 3, ... ; 20th term; 20 terms

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d and Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
Here a₁ = 9.
d = 7 - 9 = -2.
a₂₀ = 9 + (20 - 1)(-2)
a₂₀ = 9 + (19)(-2)
a₂₀ = 9 - 38 = -29
S₂₀ = (20)/(2)[2(9) + (20 - 1)(-2)]
S₂₀ = 10[18 - 38]
S₂₀ = 10(-20) = -200
Answer: 20th term = -29, sum of 20 terms = -200

Q: Q1(ii). Find the indicated term and the sum of the indicated number of terms in the arithmetic sequence: 3, (8)/(3), (7)/(3), 2, ... ; 11th term; 11 terms

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d and Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
Here a₁ = 3.
d = (8)/(3) - 3 = -(1)/(3).
a₁₁ = 3 + (11 - 1)(-(1)/(3))
a₁₁ = 3 - (10)/(3)
a₁₁ = -(1)/(3)
S₁₁ = (11)/(2)[2(3) + (11 - 1)(-(1)/(3))]
S₁₁ = (11)/(2)[6 - (10)/(3)]
S₁₁ = (11)/(2) × (8)/(3)
S₁₁ = (44)/(3)
Answer: 11th term = -(1)/(3), sum of 11 terms = (44)/(3)

Q: Q2(i). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, d and Sₙ are given. Find the ones that are missing: a₁ = 2, n = 17, d = 3

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d and Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ)
Here a₁ = 2, n = 17 and d = 3.
a₁₇ = 2 + (17 - 1)(3)
a₁₇ = 2 + (16)(3)
a₁₇ = 2 + 48 = 50
S₁₇ = (17)/(2)(2 + 50)
S₁₇ = (17)/(2)(52)
S₁₇ = 17 × 26 = 442
Answer: a₁₇ = 50, S₁₇ = 442

Q: Q2(ii). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, d and Sₙ are given. Find the ones that are missing: a₁ = -40, S₂₁ = 210

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) and aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = -40, n = 21 and S₂₁ = 210.
210 = (21)/(2)(-40 + a₂₁)
Multiply both sides by 2: 420 = 21(-40 + a₂₁)
-40 + a₂₁ = (420)/(21) = 20
a₂₁ = 20 + 40 = 60
a₂₁ = -40 + (21 - 1)d gives 60 = -40 + 20d
20d = 60 + 40 = 100
d = (100)/(20) = 5
Answer: a₂₁ = 60, d = 5, n = 21

Q: Q2(iii). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, d and Sₙ are given. Find the ones that are missing: a₁ = -7, d = 8, Sₙ = 225

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d] and aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = -7, d = 8 and Sₙ = 225.
225 = (n)/(2)[2(-7) + (n - 1)(8)]
225 = (n)/(2)[-14 + 8n - 8]
225 = (n)/(2)(8n - 22)
225 = n(4n - 11)
4n² - 11n - 225 = 0
(4n + 25)(n - 9) = 0
n = 9 (rejecting the negative value n = -(25)/(4))
a₉ = -7 + (9 - 1)(8)
a₉ = -7 + 64 = 57
Answer: n = 9, a₉ = 57

Q: Q2(iv). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, d and Sₙ are given. Find the ones that are missing: aₙ = 4, S₁₅ = 30

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) and aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here aₙ = 4, n = 15 and S₁₅ = 30.
30 = (15)/(2)(a₁ + 4)
Multiply both sides by 2: 60 = 15(a₁ + 4)
a₁ + 4 = (60)/(15) = 4
a₁ = 4 - 4 = 0
4 = 0 + (15 - 1)d gives 4 = 14d
d = (4)/(14) = (2)/(7)
Answer: n = 15, a₁ = 0, d = (2)/(7)

Q: Q3. Find the sum of all the numbers divisible by 5 from 25 through 350.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) and aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
The numbers are 25, 30, 35, ..., 350, an A.P. with a₁ = 25, d = 5, aₙ = 350.
350 = 25 + (n - 1)(5)
325 = (n - 1)(5)
n - 1 = (325)/(5) = 65
n = 66
S₆₆ = (66)/(2)(25 + 350)
S₆₆ = 33 × 375
S₆₆ = 12375
Answer: 12375

Q: Q4. The sum of three numbers in an arithmetic sequence is 36 and the sum of their cubes is 6336. Find them. [Hint: suppose the numbers are a - d, a, a + d]

Ans: Formula: for three numbers in A.P. take them as a - d, a, a + d
Sum: (a - d) + a + (a + d) = 36
3a = 36
a = 12
Sum of cubes: (a - d)³ + a³ + (a + d)³ = 6336
(a - d)³ + (a + d)³ = 2a³ + 6ad²
So 3a³ + 6ad² = 6336
Put a = 12: 3(1728) + 6(12)d² = 6336
5184 + 72d² = 6336
72d² = 6336 - 5184 = 1152
d² = (1152)/(72) = 16
d = ±4
For d = 4 the numbers are 12 - 4, 12, 12 + 4 = 8, 12, 16.
For d = -4 the numbers are 16, 12, 8.
Answer: 8, 12, 16 (or 16, 12, 8)

Q: Q5. Find four numbers in arithmetic sequence, whose sum is 20 and the sum of whose squares is 120. [Hint: suppose the numbers are a - 3d, a - d, a + d, a + 3d]

Ans: Formula: for four numbers in A.P. take them as a - 3d, a - d, a + d, a + 3d
Sum: (a - 3d) + (a - d) + (a + d) + (a + 3d) = 20
4a = 20
a = 5
Sum of squares: (a - 3d)² + (a - d)² + (a + d)² + (a + 3d)² = 120
This simplifies to 4a² + 20d² = 120.
Put a = 5: 4(25) + 20d² = 120
100 + 20d² = 120
20d² = 20
d² = 1
d = ±1
For d = 1 the numbers are 5 - 3, 5 - 1, 5 + 1, 5 + 3 = 2, 4, 6, 8.
For d = -1 the numbers are 8, 6, 4, 2.
Answer: 2, 4, 6, 8 (or 8, 6, 4, 2)

Q: Q6. x₁, x₂, x₃, ...... are in A.P. If x₁ + x₇ + x₁₀ = -6 and x₃ + x₈ + x₁₂ = -11, find x₃ + x₈ + x₂₂.

Ans: Formula: xₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d, writing a₁ for x₁
x₁ + x₇ + x₁₀ = a₁ + (a₁ + 6d) + (a₁ + 9d) = -6
3a₁ + 15d = -6 ... (i)
x₃ + x₈ + x₁₂ = (a₁ + 2d) + (a₁ + 7d) + (a₁ + 11d) = -11
3a₁ + 20d = -11 ... (ii)
Subtract (i) from (ii): 5d = -11 - (-6) = -5
d = -1
Put d = -1 in (i): 3a₁ + 15(-1) = -6
3a₁ = -6 + 15 = 9
a₁ = 3
x₃ + x₈ + x₂₂ = (a₁ + 2d) + (a₁ + 7d) + (a₁ + 21d)
= 3a₁ + 30d
= 3(3) + 30(-1)
= 9 - 30
= -21
Answer: -21

Q: Q7. Find: 1 + 3 - 5 + 7 + 9 - 11 + 13 + 15 - 17 + ... up to 3n terms.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d] for the sum of an A.P.
Group the terms in threes; 3n terms make n groups.
First group: 1 + 3 - 5 = -1
Second group: 7 + 9 - 11 = 5
Third group: 13 + 15 - 17 = 11
The group sums -1, 5, 11, ... form an A.P. with a₁ = -1 and d = 6.
Sum of n groups = (n)/(2)[2(-1) + (n - 1)(6)]
= (n)/(2)[-2 + 6n - 6]
= (n)/(2)(6n - 8)
= n(3n - 4)
Answer: n(3n - 4)

Q: Q8. Show that the sum of the first n positive odd integers is n².

Ans: Given: the first n positive odd integers 1, 3, 5, ..., (2n - 1)
To Prove: their sum is n²
The odd integers form an A.P. with a₁ = 1 and d = 2.
Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2(1) + (n - 1)(2)]
Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2 + 2n - 2]
Sₙ = (n)/(2)(2n)
Sₙ = n²
Hence proved.

Q: Q9. Find the sum of all multiples of 9 between 300 and 700.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) and aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
The multiples are 306, 315, 324, ..., 693, an A.P. with a₁ = 306, d = 9, aₙ = 693.
693 = 306 + (n - 1)(9)
387 = (n - 1)(9)
n - 1 = (387)/(9) = 43
n = 44
S₄₄ = (44)/(2)(306 + 693)
S₄₄ = 22 × 999
S₄₄ = 21978
Answer: 21978

Q: Q10. The sum of Rs.1000 is distributed among four people so that each person after the first receives Rs. 20 less than the preceding person. How much does each person receive?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
Let the first person receive a₁ rupees.
Each later person receives Rs. 20 less, so d = -20 and n = 4.
S₄ = 1000 gives (4)/(2)[2a₁ + (4 - 1)(-20)] = 1000
2[2a₁ - 60] = 1000
2a₁ - 60 = (1000)/(2) = 500
2a₁ = 500 + 60 = 560
a₁ = 280
Second person = 280 - 20 = 260
Third person = 260 - 20 = 240
Fourth person = 240 - 20 = 220
Answer: Rs.280, Rs.260, Rs.240, Rs.220

Q: Q11. The distance which an object dropped from a cliff will fall 16ft the first second, 48 ft the next second, 80 ft the third second and so on. What is the total distance the object will fall in six seconds?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
The distances 16, 48, 80, ... form an A.P.
Here a₁ = 16.
d = 48 - 16 = 32.
n = 6.
S₆ = (6)/(2)[2(16) + (6 - 1)(32)]
S₆ = 3[32 + 160]
S₆ = 3 × 192
S₆ = 576
Answer: 576 feet

Q: Q12. Afzal Khan saves Rs.1 the first day, Rs.2 the second, Rs.3 the third and Rs. n on the nth day for thirty days. How much does he save at the end of the thirtieth day?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ)
The daily savings 1, 2, 3, ..., 30 form an A.P.
Here a₁ = 1, a₃₀ = 30 and n = 30.
S₃₀ = (30)/(2)(1 + 30)
S₃₀ = 15 × 31
S₃₀ = 465
Answer: Rs.465

Q: Q13. A theater has 40 rows with 20 seats in the first row, 23 in the second row, 26 in the third row and so forth. How many seats are in the theater?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
The seats per row 20, 23, 26, ... form an A.P.
Here a₁ = 20.
d = 23 - 20 = 3.
n = 40.
S₄₀ = (40)/(2)[2(20) + (40 - 1)(3)]
S₄₀ = 20[40 + 117]
S₄₀ = 20 × 157
S₄₀ = 3140
Answer: 3140 seats

Q: Q14. Insert enough arithmetic means between 1 and 50 so that the sum of the resulting series will be 459.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) and d = (b - a)/(n + 1) for inserted means
Let N be the total number of terms of the resulting series.
Here a₁ = 1, aₙ = 50 and Sₙ = 459.
459 = (N)/(2)(1 + 50)
459 = (N)/(2)(51)
N = (459 × 2)/(51) = 18
Number of inserted means = 18 - 2 = 16.
d = (50 - 1)/(16 + 1) = (49)/(17)
First mean = 1 + (49)/(17) = (66)/(17)
Second mean = 1 + 2 × (49)/(17) = (115)/(17)
The means continue in this way up to the last mean = 50 - (49)/(17) = (801)/(17).
Answer: 16 arithmetic means, namely (66)/(17), (115)/(17), ..., (801)/(17)

mcqs.q: Four numbers in A.P. have sum 20 and sum of squares 120. In increasing order the first number is:

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The nth term of a G.P. is aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹; with a₁ = 5, r = 3 the first five terms are 5, 15, 45, 135, 405.
  • If a₃ = 27 and a₅ = 243 in a G.P., then r² = 9 and a₁ = 3.
  • A G.P. with a₁ = 16, last term (1)/(64) and r = (1)/(2) has 11 terms.
  • x + 7, x - 3, x - 8 are in G.P. when x = 13, giving the sequence 20, 10, 5.
  • The geometric mean of a and b is G = ±√(ab); for -6 and -216, G = ±36.
  • For √2 + 3 and √2 - 3 the product is -7, so no real geometric mean exists.
  • Five geometric means between (32)/(9) and (81)/(2) are (16)/(3), 8, 12, 18, 27, with r = (3)/(2).

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Write the first five terms of a geometric sequence given that: a₁ = 5; r = 3

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
Here a₁ = 5 and r = 3.
a₁ = 5
a₂ = 5 × 3 = 15
a₃ = 5 × 3² = 5 × 9 = 45
a₄ = 5 × 3³ = 5 × 27 = 135
a₅ = 5 × 3⁴ = 5 × 81 = 405
Answer: 5, 15, 45, 135, 405

Q: Q1(ii). Write the first five terms of a geometric sequence given that: a₁ = 8; r = -(1)/(2)

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
Here a₁ = 8 and r = -(1)/(2).
a₁ = 8
a₂ = 8 × (-(1)/(2)) = -4
a₃ = 8 × (-(1)/(2))² = 8 × (1)/(4) = 2
a₄ = 8 × (-(1)/(2))³ = 8 × (-(1)/(8)) = -1
a₅ = 8 × (-(1)/(2))⁴ = 8 × (1)/(16) = (1)/(2)
Answer: 8, -4, 2, -1, (1)/(2)

Q: Q1(iii). Write the first five terms of a geometric sequence given that: a₁ = -(9)/(16); r = -(2)/(3)

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
Here a₁ = -(9)/(16) and r = -(2)/(3).
a₁ = -(9)/(16)
a₂ = (-(9)/(16)) × (-(2)/(3)) = (3)/(8)
a₃ = (-(9)/(16)) × (-(2)/(3))² = (-(9)/(16)) × (4)/(9) = -(1)/(4)
a₄ = (-(9)/(16)) × (-(2)/(3))³ = (-(9)/(16)) × (-(8)/(27)) = (1)/(6)
a₅ = (-(9)/(16)) × (-(2)/(3))⁴ = (-(9)/(16)) × (16)/(81) = -(1)/(9)
Answer: -(9)/(16), (3)/(8), -(1)/(4), (1)/(6), -(1)/(9)

Q: Q1(iv). Write the first five terms of a geometric sequence given that: a₁ = (x)/(y); r = -(y)/(x)

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
Here a₁ = (x)/(y) and r = -(y)/(x).
a₁ = (x)/(y)
a₂ = (x)/(y) × (-(y)/(x)) = -1
a₃ = (x)/(y) × (-(y)/(x))² = (x)/(y) × (y²)/(x²) = (y)/(x)
a₄ = (x)/(y) × (-(y)/(x))³ = (x)/(y) × (-(y³)/(x³)) = -(y²)/(x²)
a₅ = (x)/(y) × (-(y)/(x))⁴ = (x)/(y) × (y⁴)/(x⁴) = (y³)/(x³)
Answer: (x)/(y), -1, (y)/(x), -(y²)/(x²), (y³)/(x³)

Q: Q2. Suppose that the third term of a geometric sequence is 27 and the fifth term is 243. Find the first term and common ratio of the sequence.

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
a₃ = a₁r² = 27 ... (i)
a₅ = a₁r⁴ = 243 ... (ii)
Divide (ii) by (i): (a₁r⁴)/(a₁r²) = (243)/(27)
r² = 9
r = ±3
Put r² = 9 in (i): a₁ × 9 = 27
a₁ = (27)/(9) = 3
Answer: a₁ = 3, r = ±3

Q: Q3. Find the seventh term of a geometric sequence that has 2 and -√2 for its second and third terms respectively.

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ and r = (a₃)/(a₂)
Here a₂ = 2 and a₃ = -√2.
r = (-√2)/(2) = -(1)/(√2)
a₇ = a₂ × r⁵, going from the 2nd term to the 7th term in 5 steps.
r⁵ = (-(1)/(√2))⁵ = -(1)/(4√2)
a₇ = 2 × (-(1)/(4√2))
a₇ = -(1)/(2√2)
Rationalising: a₇ = -(√2)/(4), which is -2^(-3/2).
Answer: -(√2)/(4)

Q: Q4. How many terms are there in a geometric sequence in which the first and the last terms are 16 and (1)/(64) respectively and r = (1)/(2)?

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
Here a₁ = 16, aₙ = (1)/(64) and r = (1)/(2).
(1)/(64) = 16 × ((1)/(2))ⁿ⁻¹
((1)/(2))ⁿ⁻¹ = ((1)/(64))/(16) = (1)/(1024)
((1)/(2))ⁿ⁻¹ = ((1)/(2))¹⁰, since 2¹⁰ = 1024.
n - 1 = 10
n = 11
Answer: 11 terms

Q: Q5. Find x so that x + 7, x - 3, x - 8 form a three term geometric sequence in the given order. Also give the sequence.

Ans: Formula: if p, q, s are in G.P. then q² = ps
Here p = x + 7, q = x - 3, s = x - 8.
(x - 3)² = (x + 7)(x - 8)
x² - 6x + 9 = x² - x - 56
-6x + 9 = -x - 56
-6x + x = -56 - 9
-5x = -65
x = (65)/(5) = 13
First term = 13 + 7 = 20
Second term = 13 - 3 = 10
Third term = 13 - 8 = 5
Answer: x = 13; the sequence is 20, 10, 5

Q: Q6. If a₁₀ = l, a₁₃ = m, a₁₆ = n; show that ln = m²

Ans: Given: a₁₀ = l, a₁₃ = m, a₁₆ = n for a geometric sequence
To Prove: ln = m²
Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹
l = a₁₀ = a₁r⁹
m = a₁₃ = a₁r¹²
n = a₁₆ = a₁r¹⁵
ln = (a₁r⁹)(a₁r¹⁵)
ln = a₁²r²⁴
m² = (a₁r¹²)²
m² = a₁²r²⁴
So ln = m².
Hence proved.

Q: Q7. Show that the reciprocals of the terms of a geometric sequence also form a geometric sequence.

Ans: Given: a geometric sequence a₁, a₁r, a₁r², a₁r³, ... with common ratio r
To Prove: the reciprocals (1)/(a₁), (1)/(a₁r), (1)/(a₁r²), ... form a geometric sequence
Ratio of the 2nd reciprocal to the 1st: ((1)/(a₁r))/((1)/(a₁)) = (a₁)/(a₁r) = (1)/(r)
Ratio of the 3rd reciprocal to the 2nd: ((1)/(a₁r²))/((1)/(a₁r)) = (a₁r)/(a₁r²) = (1)/(r)
Every ratio of successive reciprocals is the same constant (1)/(r).
So the reciprocals form a geometric sequence with common ratio (1)/(r).
Hence proved.

Q: Q8(i). Find the geometric mean of the following: 3.14 and 2.71

Ans: Formula: G = ±√(ab)
Here a = 3.14 and b = 2.71.
ab = 3.14 × 2.71 = 8.5094
G = ±√(8.5094)
G ≈ ±2.92
Answer: 2.92 or -2.92 (approximately)

Q: Q8(ii). Find the geometric mean of the following: -6 and -216

Ans: Formula: G = ±√(ab)
Here a = -6 and b = -216.
ab = (-6) × (-216) = 1296
G = ±√(1296)
G = ±36
Answer: 36 or -36

Q: Q8(iii). Find the geometric mean of the following: x + y and x - y

Ans: Formula: G = ±√(ab)
Here a = x + y and b = x - y.
ab = (x + y)(x - y) = x² - y²
G = ±√(x² - y²)
Answer: ±√(x² - y²)

Q: Q8(iv). Find the geometric mean of the following: √2 + 3 and √2 - 3

Ans: Formula: G = ±√(ab)
Here a = √2 + 3 and b = √2 - 3.
ab = (√2 + 3)(√2 - 3)
ab = (√2)² - 3²
ab = 2 - 9 = -7
G = ±√(-7)
The product is negative, so no real square root exists.
Answer: The geometric mean does not exist (in real numbers)

Q: Q9(i). Insert 5 geometric means between 3(5)/(9) and 40(1)/(2).

Ans: Formula: r = ((b)/(a))^(1/(n + 1)) for n geometric means between a and b, and Gₖ = a₁rᵏ
Here a = 3(5)/(9) = (32)/(9), b = 40(1)/(2) = (81)/(2) and n = 5.
(b)/(a) = ((81)/(2))/((32)/(9)) = (81 × 9)/(2 × 32) = (729)/(64)
r = ((729)/(64))^(1/(6)) = (3)/(2), since (3)/(2)⁶ = (729)/(64).
G₁ = (32)/(9) × (3)/(2) = (16)/(3)
G₂ = (32)/(9) × ((3)/(2))² = 8
G₃ = (32)/(9) × ((3)/(2))³ = 12
G₄ = (32)/(9) × ((3)/(2))⁴ = 18
G₅ = (32)/(9) × ((3)/(2))⁵ = 27
Answer: (16)/(3), 8, 12, 18, 27

Q: Q9(ii). Insert 6 geometric means between 14 and -(7)/(64).

Ans: Formula: r = ((b)/(a))^(1/(n + 1)) for n geometric means between a and b, and Gₖ = a₁rᵏ
Here a = 14, b = -(7)/(64) and n = 6.
(b)/(a) = (-(7)/(64))/(14) = -(1)/(128)
r = (-(1)/(128))^(1/(7)) = -(1)/(2), since (-(1)/(2))⁷ = -(1)/(128).
G₁ = 14 × (-(1)/(2)) = -7
G₂ = 14 × (-(1)/(2))² = (7)/(2)
G₃ = 14 × (-(1)/(2))³ = -(7)/(4)
G₄ = 14 × (-(1)/(2))⁴ = (7)/(8)
G₅ = 14 × (-(1)/(2))⁵ = -(7)/(16)
G₆ = 14 × (-(1)/(2))⁶ = (7)/(32)
Answer: -7, (7)/(2), -(7)/(4), (7)/(8), -(7)/(16), (7)/(32)

Q: Q10. Find two numbers if the difference between them is 48 and their A.M. exceeds their G.M. by 18.

Ans: Formula: A.M. = (a + b)/(2) and G.M. = √(ab)
Let the numbers be a and b with a - b = 48.
(a + b)/(2) - √(ab) = 18 ... (i)
Let s = a + b and p = ab.
Then (s)/(2) - √(p) = 18, so s = 36 + 2√(p).
Also s² = (a - b)² + 4p = 48² + 4p = 2304 + 4p.
Put t = √(p), so s = 36 + 2t and s² = 2304 + 4t².
(36 + 2t)² = 2304 + 4t²
1296 + 144t + 4t² = 2304 + 4t²
144t = 2304 - 1296 = 1008
t = (1008)/(144) = 7
So p = 49 and s = 36 + 2(7) = 50.
a and b are the roots of x² - 50x + 49 = 0.
(x - 49)(x - 1) = 0
x = 49 or x = 1
Check: 49 - 1 = 48 and (49 + 1)/(2) - √(49) = 25 - 7 = 18. Correct.
Answer: 49 and 1

Q: Q11. Prove that the product of n geometric means between a and b is equal to the nth power of the single geometric mean between them.

Ans: Given: G₁, G₂, ..., Gₙ are the n geometric means between a and b
To Prove: G₁G₂...Gₙ = Gⁿ, where G = √(ab) is the single geometric mean between a and b
Formula: Gₖ = a((b)/(a))^(k/(n + 1)) for k = 1, 2, ..., n
Product = aⁿ × ((b)/(a))^((1 + 2 + ... + n)/(n + 1))
1 + 2 + ... + n = (n(n + 1))/(2)
So the exponent is (n(n + 1)/(2))/(n + 1) = (n)/(2).
Product = aⁿ × ((b)/(a))^(n/(2))
= aⁿ × (b^(n/(2)))/(a^(n/(2)))
= a^(n/(2)) b^(n/(2))
= (ab)^(n/(2))
= (√(ab))ⁿ = Gⁿ
Hence proved.

Q: Q12. For what value of n, (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) is the geometric mean between a and b?

Ans: Formula: the geometric mean between a and b is √(ab)
Set (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) = √(ab)
Cross-multiplying: aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹ = √(ab)(aⁿ + bⁿ)
aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹ = aⁿ⁺¹ᐟ²b¹ᐟ² + a¹ᐟ²bⁿ⁺¹ᐟ², writing √(ab) × aⁿ = a^(n + (1)/(2)) b^((1)/(2)) and similarly for the other term.
aⁿ⁺¹ - a^(n + (1)/(2)) b^((1)/(2)) = a^((1)/(2)) b^(n + (1)/(2)) - bⁿ⁺¹
a^(n + (1)/(2))(a^((1)/(2)) - b^((1)/(2))) = b^(n + (1)/(2))(a^((1)/(2)) - b^((1)/(2)))
Since a ≠ b, divide by (a^((1)/(2)) - b^((1)/(2))): a^(n + (1)/(2)) = b^(n + (1)/(2))
This holds when n + (1)/(2) = 0.
n = -(1)/(2)
Answer: n = -(1)/(2)

mcqs.why: Use aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹. a₅ = 5 × 3⁴ = 5 × 81 = 405.

mcqs.q: If a₁ = 8 and r = -(1)/(2) in a G.P., then a₅ =
If a₃ = 27 and a₅ = 243 in a G.P., then a₁ =
mcqs.why: Divide: r² = (a₅)/(a₃) = (243)/(27) = 9. Then a₃ = a₁r² gives 27 = a₁ × 9, so a₁ = (27)/(9) = 3.

mcqs.q: A G.P. has a₁ = 16, last term (1)/(64) and r = (1)/(2). The number of terms is:
x + 7, x - 3, x - 8 are in G.P. when x =
mcqs.why: For a G.P., (x - 3)² = (x + 7)(x - 8). Expanding: x² - 6x + 9 = x² - x - 56, so -5x = -65 and x = 13, giving 20, 10, 5.

mcqs.q: The positive geometric mean of -6 and -216 is:
mcqs.why: Use G = √(ab). ab = (-6) × (-216) = 1296. G = √(1296) = 36 (the full geometric mean is ±36).

mcqs.q: The geometric mean of √2 + 3 and √2 - 3 in real numbers:
mcqs.why: Use G = ±√(ab). ab = (√2 + 3)(√2 - 3) = 2 - 9 = -7. The product is negative, so no real square root exists and the geometric mean does not exist in real numbers.

mcqs.q: The third of five geometric means between (32)/(9) and (81)/(2) is:
The first of six geometric means between 14 and -(7)/(64) is:
Two numbers differ by 48 and their A.M. exceeds their G.M. by 18. The larger number is:
mcqs.why: Let s = a + b and t = √(ab). Then (s)/(2) - t = 18 and s² = 48² + 4t². Solving gives t = 7, s = 50, so the numbers satisfy x² - 50x + 49 = 0, giving 49 and 1. The larger is 49.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1) for r > 1 and Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r); 3 + 6 + 12 + ... + 3·2⁹ = 3069.
  • 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + ... + (1)/(16) = (255)/(16) over 8 terms.
  • For |r| < 1 the infinite sum is S = (a₁)/(1 - r); (8)/(5), -1, (5)/(8), ... sums to (64)/(65).
  • Recurring decimals are infinite G.P.s: 0.888... = (8)/(9) and 1.636363... = (18)/(11).
  • S₁₀ = 244S₅ in a G.P. gives r⁵ + 1 = 244, so r = 3.
  • Three numbers in G.P. with sum 38 and product 1728 are 8, 12, 18.
  • S₆ = 9S₃ in a geometric series gives r³ + 1 = 9, so r = 2.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Compute the sum: 3 + 6 + 12 + ... + 3.2⁹

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1) for r > 1
The terms are 3 × 2⁰, 3 × 2¹, ..., 3 × 2⁹, so a₁ = 3, r = 2 and n = 10.
S₁₀ = (3(2¹⁰ - 1))/(2 - 1)
S₁₀ = 3(1024 - 1)
S₁₀ = 3 × 1023
S₁₀ = 3069
Answer: 3(2¹⁰ - 1) = 3069

Q: Q1(ii). Compute the sum: 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + ... + (1)/(16)

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r) for |r| < 1
Here a₁ = 8 and r = (4)/(8) = (1)/(2).
Find n from the last term: 8 × ((1)/(2))ⁿ⁻¹ = (1)/(16)
((1)/(2))ⁿ⁻¹ = (1)/(128) = ((1)/(2))⁷
n - 1 = 7, so n = 8.
S₈ = (8(1 - ((1)/(2))⁸))/(1 - (1)/(2))
S₈ = (8(1 - (1)/(256)))/((1)/(2))
S₈ = 16 × (255)/(256)
S₈ = (255)/(16)
Answer: (255)/(16)
Note: The book's printed answer ((255)/(7)) is incorrect; the correct answer is (255)/(16).

Q: Q1(iii). Compute the sum: 2⁴ + 2⁵ + 2⁶ + ... + 2¹⁰

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1) for r > 1
Here a₁ = 2⁴ = 16, r = 2 and the terms run from 2⁴ to 2¹⁰, so n = 7.
S₇ = (16(2⁷ - 1))/(2 - 1)
S₇ = 16(128 - 1)
S₇ = 16 × 127
S₇ = 2032
Answer: 2032

Q: Q1(iv). Compute the sum: (8)/(5), -1, (5)/(8), ...

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
Here a₁ = (8)/(5).
r = (-1)/((8)/(5)) = -(5)/(8)
|r| = (5)/(8) < 1, so the infinite sum exists.
S = ((8)/(5))/(1 - (-(5)/(8)))
S = ((8)/(5))/((13)/(8))
S = (8)/(5) × (8)/(13)
S = (64)/(65)
Answer: (64)/(65)

Q: Q1(v). Compute the sum: 2, (2)/(√2), 1, (1)/(√2), (1)/(2), ...

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
Here a₁ = 2.
r = ((2)/(√2))/(2) = (1)/(√2)
|r| = (1)/(√2) < 1, so the infinite sum exists.
S = (2)/(1 - (1)/(√2))
S = (2√2)/(√2 - 1)
Rationalising by multiplying numerator and denominator by (√2 + 1): S = (2√2(√2 + 1))/((√2 - 1)(√2 + 1))
S = (2√2(√2 + 1))/(1)
S = 4 + 2√2
Answer: 4 + 2√2

Q: Q1(vi). Compute the sum: -(1)/(3), (1)/(2), -(3)/(4), ............ to 7 terms.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r), r ≠ 1
Here a₁ = -(1)/(3).
r = ((1)/(2))/(-(1)/(3)) = -(3)/(2)
n = 7.
S₇ = ((-(1)/(3))(1 - (-(3)/(2))⁷))/(1 - (-(3)/(2)))
(-(3)/(2))⁷ = -(2187)/(128)
1 - (-(2187)/(128)) = (2315)/(128)
1 - (-(3)/(2)) = (5)/(2)
S₇ = ((-(1)/(3)) × (2315)/(128))/((5)/(2))
S₇ = -(1)/(3) × (2315)/(128) × (2)/(5)
S₇ = -(463)/(192)
Answer: -(463)/(192)

Q: Q2(i). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, r and Sₙ of a geometric sequence are given. Find the ones that are missing: a₁ = 1, r = -2, aₙ = 64

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ and Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r)
Here a₁ = 1, r = -2 and aₙ = 64.
64 = 1 × (-2)ⁿ⁻¹
(-2)ⁿ⁻¹ = 64 = (-2)⁶
n - 1 = 6
n = 7
S₇ = (1(1 - (-2)⁷))/(1 - (-2))
S₇ = (1 - (-128))/(3)
S₇ = (129)/(3) = 43
Answer: n = 7, S₇ = 43

Q: Q2(ii). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, r and Sₙ of a geometric sequence are given. Find the ones that are missing: r = (1)/(2), a₉ = 1

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ and Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r)
Here r = (1)/(2), n = 9 and a₉ = 1.
1 = a₁ × ((1)/(2))⁸
a₁ = 1 × 2⁸ = 256
S₉ = (256(1 - ((1)/(2))⁹))/(1 - (1)/(2))
S₉ = (256(1 - (1)/(512)))/((1)/(2))
S₉ = 512 × (511)/(512)
S₉ = 511
Answer: n = 9, a₁ = 256, S₉ = 511

Q: Q2(iii). Some of the components a₁, aₙ, n, r and Sₙ of a geometric sequence are given. Find the ones that are missing: r = -2, Sₙ = -63, aₙ = -96

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ and Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r)
Here r = -2, Sₙ = -63 and aₙ = -96.
From Sₙ: -63 = (a₁(1 - (-2)ⁿ))/(1 - (-2)) = (a₁(1 - (-2)ⁿ))/(3)
So a₁(1 - (-2)ⁿ) = -189 ... (i)
From aₙ: a₁(-2)ⁿ⁻¹ = -96 ... (ii)
Try n = 6 in (i): a₁(1 - 64) = -189
-63a₁ = -189
a₁ = 3
Check in (ii): a₆ = 3 × (-2)⁵ = 3 × (-32) = -96. Correct.
Answer: a₁ = 3, n = 6

Q: Q3. Find the first five terms and the sum of an infinite geometric sequence having a₂ = 2 and a₃ = 1

Ans: Formula: r = (a₃)/(a₂), aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ and S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1
r = (1)/(2)
a₂ = a₁r gives 2 = a₁ × (1)/(2)
a₁ = 4
First term = 4
Second term = 2
Third term = 1
Fourth term = 4 × ((1)/(2))³ = (1)/(2)
Fifth term = 4 × ((1)/(2))⁴ = (1)/(4)
|r| = (1)/(2) < 1, so the infinite sum exists.
S = (4)/(1 - (1)/(2))
S = (4)/((1)/(2)) = 8
Answer: The first five terms are 4, 2, 1, (1)/(2), (1)/(4); S = 8

Q: Q4(i). Find the value of: 0.8 (the digit 8 is recurring, i.e. 0.888...)

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
0.888... = 0.8 + 0.08 + 0.008 + ...
This is an infinite geometric series with a₁ = 0.8 and r = 0.1.
S = (0.8)/(1 - 0.1)
S = (0.8)/(0.9)
S = (8)/(9)
Answer: (8)/(9)

Q: Q4(ii). Find the value of: 1.63 (the digits 63 are recurring, i.e. 1.636363...)

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
1.636363... = 1 + 0.636363...
0.636363... = 0.63 + 0.0063 + 0.000063 + ..., an infinite geometric series with a₁ = 0.63 and r = 0.01.
Sum of the recurring part = (0.63)/(1 - 0.01) = (0.63)/(0.99) = (63)/(99) = (7)/(11)
Total = 1 + (7)/(11)
= (18)/(11)
Answer: (18)/(11)

Q: Q4(iii). Find the value of: 2.15 (only the digit 5 is recurring, i.e. 2.1555...)

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
2.1555... = 2.1 + 0.0555...
0.0555... = 0.05 + 0.005 + 0.0005 + ..., an infinite geometric series with a₁ = 0.05 and r = 0.1.
Sum of the recurring part = (0.05)/(1 - 0.1) = (0.05)/(0.9) = (5)/(90) = (1)/(18)
Total = 2.1 + (1)/(18)
= (21)/(10) + (1)/(18)
= (189 + 5)/(90)
= (194)/(90) = (97)/(45)
Answer: (97)/(45)

Q: Q4(iv). Find the value of: 0.123 (the digits 123 are recurring, i.e. 0.123123123...)

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
0.123123... = 0.123 + 0.000123 + 0.000000123 + ...
This is an infinite geometric series with a₁ = 0.123 and r = 0.001.
S = (0.123)/(1 - 0.001)
S = (0.123)/(0.999)
S = (123)/(999)
S = (41)/(333)
Answer: (41)/(333)

Q: Q5. Find r such that: S₁₀ = 244S₅.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1), r ≠ 1
S₁₀ = (a₁(r¹⁰ - 1))/(r - 1) and S₅ = (a₁(r⁵ - 1))/(r - 1).
S₁₀ = 244S₅ gives (r¹⁰ - 1)/(r⁵ - 1) = 244
r¹⁰ - 1 = (r⁵ - 1)(r⁵ + 1), so (r¹⁰ - 1)/(r⁵ - 1) = r⁵ + 1.
r⁵ + 1 = 244
r⁵ = 243
r⁵ = 3⁵
r = 3
Answer: r = 3

Q: Q6. Prove that: Sₙ(S₃ₙ - S₂ₙ) = (Sₙ - S₂ₙ)²

Ans: Given: Sₙ, S₂ₙ, S₃ₙ are the sums of the first n, 2n, 3n terms of a geometric series
To Prove: Sₙ(S₃ₙ - S₂ₙ) = (Sₙ - S₂ₙ)²
Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r)
S₂ₙ - Sₙ = sum of the next n terms = a₁rⁿ(1 + r + ... + rⁿ⁻¹) = rⁿSₙ
So Sₙ - S₂ₙ = -rⁿSₙ ... (i)
S₃ₙ - S₂ₙ = sum of the n terms after the first 2n terms = a₁r²ⁿ(1 + r + ... + rⁿ⁻¹) = r²ⁿSₙ ... (ii)
Left side = Sₙ × r²ⁿSₙ = r²ⁿSₙ² (using (ii))
Right side = (-rⁿSₙ)² = r²ⁿSₙ² (using (i))
Left side = Right side.
Hence proved.

Q: Q7. Find the sum Sₙ of the first n terms of the sequence {((1)/(2))ⁿ}.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r), r ≠ 1
The sequence is (1)/(2), (1)/(4), (1)/(8), ..., a geometric sequence.
Here a₁ = (1)/(2) and r = (1)/(2).
Sₙ = (((1)/(2))(1 - ((1)/(2))ⁿ))/(1 - (1)/(2))
Sₙ = (((1)/(2))(1 - (1)/(2ⁿ)))/((1)/(2))
Sₙ = 1 - (1)/(2ⁿ)
Answer: Sₙ = 1 - (1)/(2ⁿ)

Q: Q8. The sum of three numbers in G. P. is 38, and their product is 1728; find them.

Ans: Formula: for three numbers in G.P. take them as (a)/(r), a, ar; their product is a³
Product: ((a)/(r)) × a × (ar) = 1728
a³ = 1728
a = 12, since 12³ = 1728.
Sum: (12)/(r) + 12 + 12r = 38
(12)/(r) + 12r = 38 - 12 = 26
Divide by 2: (6)/(r) + 6r = 13
Multiply by r: 6 + 6r² = 13r
6r² - 13r + 6 = 0
(3r - 2)(2r - 3) = 0
r = (2)/(3) or r = (3)/(2)
For r = (3)/(2): the numbers are 12 × (2)/(3), 12, 12 × (3)/(2) = 8, 12, 18.
For r = (2)/(3): the numbers are 18, 12, 8.
Answer: 8, 12, 18 (or 18, 12, 8)

Q: Q9. The sum of first 6 terms of a geometric series is 9 times the sum of its first three terms. Find the common ratio.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1), r ≠ 1
Given: S₆ = 9S₃
(a₁(r⁶ - 1))/(r - 1) = 9 × (a₁(r³ - 1))/(r - 1)
(r⁶ - 1)/(r³ - 1) = 9
r⁶ - 1 = (r³ - 1)(r³ + 1), so (r⁶ - 1)/(r³ - 1) = r³ + 1.
r³ + 1 = 9
r³ = 8
r³ = 2³
r = 2
Answer: r = 2

Q: Q10. How many terms of the series: 1 + √3 + 3 + .... be added to get the sum 40 + 13√3.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1) for r > 1
Here a₁ = 1 and r = √3.
Sₙ = (1 × ((√3)ⁿ - 1))/(√3 - 1) = 40 + 13√3
Try n = 7: the terms are 1, √3, 3, 3√3, 9, 9√3, 27.
Rational part: 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 = 40
√3 part: √3 + 3√3 + 9√3 = 13√3
Sum = 40 + 13√3, as required.
Answer: 7 terms

Q: Q11. If pth, qth, rth terms of a G. P. be a, b, c respectively, prove that a^(q - r) b^(r - p) c^(p - q) = 1.

Ans: Given: the pth, qth, rth terms of a G.P. are a, b, c respectively
To Prove: a^(q - r) b^(r - p) c^(p - q) = 1
Formula: Tₙ = ARⁿ⁻¹, where A is the first term and R the common ratio
Let the G.P. have first term A and common ratio R.
Then a = AR^(p - 1), b = AR^(q - 1), c = AR^(r - 1).
a^(q - r) = A^(q - r) R^((p - 1)(q - r))
b^(r - p) = A^(r - p) R^((q - 1)(r - p))
c^(p - q) = A^(p - q) R^((r - 1)(p - q))
Exponent of A in the product: (q - r) + (r - p) + (p - q) = 0
Exponent of R in the product: (p - 1)(q - r) + (q - 1)(r - p) + (r - 1)(p - q)
Expanding: (pq - pr - q + r) + (qr - pq - r + p) + (rp - qr - p + q) = 0
So the product = A⁰ × R⁰ = 1 × 1 = 1.
Hence proved.

Q: Q12. Find an infinite geometric series whose sum is 6 and such that each term is four times the sum of all the terms that follow it.

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1
Let the series have first term a₁ and common ratio r, with sum 6.
(a₁)/(1 - r) = 6 ... (i)
Each term is four times the sum of all the terms after it.
For the first term: a₁ = 4 × (sum of all later terms) = 4(6 - a₁)
a₁ = 24 - 4a₁
5a₁ = 24
a₁ = (24)/(5)
Put a₁ = (24)/(5) in (i): ((24)/(5))/(1 - r) = 6
1 - r = ((24)/(5))/(6) = (4)/(5)
r = 1 - (4)/(5) = (1)/(5)
The series is (24)/(5) + (24)/(5²) + (24)/(5³) + ...
Answer: a₁ = (24)/(5), r = (1)/(5); the series is (24)/(5) + (24)/(5²) + ...

Q: Q13. If y = (x)/(3) + (x²)/(3²) + (x³)/(3³) + ..., where 0 < x < 3, then show that x = (3y)/(1 + y)

Ans: Given: y = (x)/(3) + (x²)/(3²) + (x³)/(3³) + ..., where 0 < x < 3
To Prove: x = (3y)/(1 + y)
The right side is an infinite geometric series.
Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1
Here a₁ = (x)/(3) and r = ((x²)/(3²))/((x)/(3)) = (x)/(3).
Since 0 < x < 3, |r| = (x)/(3) < 1, so the sum exists.
y = ((x)/(3))/(1 - (x)/(3))
y = ((x)/(3))/((3 - x)/(3)) = (x)/(3 - x)
y(3 - x) = x
3y - xy = x
3y = x + xy
3y = x(1 + y)
x = (3y)/(1 + y)
Hence proved.

Q: Q14. A ball rebounds to half the height from which it is dropped. If it is dropped from 10 ft, how far does it travel from the moment it is dropped until the moment of its eighth bounce?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r) for |r| < 1
The ball first falls 10 ft.
It rebounds to (1)/(2) × 10 = 5 ft, then falls 5 ft, and so on.
Up to the moment of the eighth bounce it makes 7 complete up-and-down rebounds, of heights 5, (5)/(2), (5)/(4), ..., 10 × ((1)/(2))⁷ ft.
The rebound distances form a geometric series with a₁ = 2 × 5 = 10 (up and down), r = (1)/(2) and n = 7.
Sum of rebound distances = (10(1 - ((1)/(2))⁷))/(1 - (1)/(2))
= (10(1 - (1)/(128)))/((1)/(2))
= 20 × (127)/(128)
= (635)/(32) ft
Total distance = initial fall + rebound distances
= 10 + (635)/(32)
= (955)/(32)
= 29(27)/(32) ft
Answer: 29(27)/(32) ft

Q: Q15. A man wishes to save money by setting aside Rs.1 the first day, Rs.2 the second day, Rs.4 the third day and so on, doubling the amount each day. If this continued, how much must be set aside on the 15th day? What is the total amount saved at the end of 30 days?

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ and Sₙ = (a₁(rⁿ - 1))/(r - 1) for r > 1
The daily amounts 1, 2, 4, ... form a G.P. with a₁ = 1 and r = 2.
Amount on the 15th day: a₁₅ = 1 × 2¹⁴
2¹⁴ = 16384
a₁₅ = Rs.16384
Total saved in 30 days: S₃₀ = (1 × (2³⁰ - 1))/(2 - 1)
S₃₀ = 2³⁰ - 1
2³⁰ = 1073741824
S₃₀ = 1073741824 - 1 = Rs.1073741823
Answer: Rs.16384 on the 15th day; total saved Rs.1073741823

Q: Q16. The number of bacteria in a culture increased geometrically from 64000 to 729000 in 6 days. Find the daily rate of increase if the rate is assumed to be constant.

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹ for a geometric sequence
Let r be the daily multiplying factor.
In 6 days the number is multiplied by r⁶.
64000 × r⁶ = 729000
r⁶ = (729000)/(64000) = (729)/(64)
(729)/(64) = ((3)/(2))⁶, since 3⁶ = 729 and 2⁶ = 64.
r = (3)/(2)
So each day the number becomes (3)/(2) times the previous day's number.
The daily increase is (3)/(2) - 1 = (1)/(2) of the previous number, i.e. 50% per day.
Answer: The daily multiplying factor is (3)/(2), i.e. an increase of 50% per day

lessons.title: Exercise 4.6
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • The nth term of an H.P. is the reciprocal of the nth term of the corresponding A.P. of reciprocals.
  • For (1)/(2), (1)/(5), (1)/(8), ... the 9th term is (1)/(26); for 6, 2, (6)/(5), ... the 20th term is (2)/(13).
  • A = (a + b)/(2), H = (2ab)/(a + b), G = ±√(ab), and G² = A × H always.
  • For 3.14 and 2.71: A = 2.925, G ≈ ±2.92, H ≈ 2.91.
  • (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) is the harmonic mean between a and b when n = -1.
  • Two harmonic means between 12 and 48 are 16 and 24.
  • If A = 8 and H = 6, the two numbers are 4 and 12; if H = (24)/(5) and G = 6, the numbers are 3 and 12.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the indicated term of the harmonic progression: (1)/(2), (1)/(5), (1)/(8), ...; 9th term

Ans: Formula: the nth term of an H.P. is (1)/(a₁ + (n - 1)d), where a₁ and d belong to the corresponding A.P. of reciprocals
The reciprocals are 2, 5, 8, ..., an A.P. with a₁ = 2 and d = 3.
9th term of the A.P. = 2 + (9 - 1)(3)
= 2 + 24 = 26
So the 9th term of the H.P. is its reciprocal.
Answer: (1)/(26)

Q: Q1(ii). Find the indicated term of the harmonic progression: 6, 2, (6)/(5), ...; 20th term

Ans: Formula: the nth term of an H.P. is (1)/(a₁ + (n - 1)d), where a₁ and d belong to the corresponding A.P. of reciprocals
The reciprocals are (1)/(6), (1)/(2), (5)/(6), ..., an A.P.
d = (1)/(2) - (1)/(6) = (1)/(3)
20th term of the A.P. = (1)/(6) + (20 - 1) × (1)/(3)
= (1)/(6) + (19)/(3)
= (1)/(6) + (38)/(6) = (39)/(6) = (13)/(2)
So the 20th term of the H.P. is its reciprocal.
Answer: (2)/(13)

Q: Q1(iii). Find the indicated term of the harmonic progression: 5(2)/(3), 3(2)/(5), 2(3)/(7), ...; 8th term

Ans: Formula: the nth term of an H.P. is (1)/(a₁ + (n - 1)d), where a₁ and d belong to the corresponding A.P. of reciprocals
Write the terms as (17)/(3), (17)/(5), (17)/(7), ...
The reciprocals are (3)/(17), (5)/(17), (7)/(17), ..., an A.P.
d = (5)/(17) - (3)/(17) = (2)/(17)
8th term of the A.P. = (3)/(17) + (8 - 1) × (2)/(17)
= (3)/(17) + (14)/(17)
= (17)/(17) = 1
So the 8th term of the H.P. is its reciprocal, (1)/(1).
Answer: 1

Q: Q2. Find five more terms of the H.P. (1)/(3), 1, -1, ...

Ans: Formula: the terms of an H.P. are found from the corresponding A.P. of reciprocals, aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
The reciprocals are 3, 1, -1, ..., an A.P. with a₁ = 3 and d = 1 - 3 = -2.
4th term of the A.P. = 3 + (4 - 1)(-2) = -3
5th term of the A.P. = 3 + (5 - 1)(-2) = -5
6th term of the A.P. = 3 + (6 - 1)(-2) = -7
7th term of the A.P. = 3 + (7 - 1)(-2) = -9
8th term of the A.P. = 3 + (8 - 1)(-2) = -11
Taking reciprocals gives the next five terms of the H.P.
Answer: -(1)/(3), -(1)/(5), -(1)/(7), -(1)/(9), -(1)/(11)

Q: Q3. The second term of an H.P is (1)/(2) and the fifth term is -(1)/(4). Find the 12th term.

Ans: Formula: the nth term of an H.P. is (1)/(a₁ + (n - 1)d), where a₁ and d belong to the corresponding A.P. of reciprocals
The reciprocals of the 2nd and 5th terms are 2 and -4.
For the corresponding A.P.: a₁ + d = 2 ... (i)
a₁ + 4d = -4 ... (ii)
Subtract (i) from (ii): 3d = -4 - 2 = -6
d = -2
From (i): a₁ = 2 - d = 2 - (-2) = 4
12th term of the A.P. = 4 + (12 - 1)(-2)
= 4 - 22 = -18
So the 12th term of the H.P. is its reciprocal.
Answer: -(1)/(18)

Q: Q4(i). Find the arithmetic, harmonic and geometric means of: 3.14 and 2.71. Also verify that A × H = G².

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2), H = (2ab)/(a + b), G = ±√(ab)
Here a = 3.14 and b = 2.71.
A = (3.14 + 2.71)/(2) = (5.85)/(2) = 2.925
ab = 3.14 × 2.71 = 8.5094
G = ±√(8.5094) ≈ ±2.92
H = (2 × 8.5094)/(5.85) = (17.0188)/(5.85) ≈ 2.91
Verification: A × H ≈ 2.925 × 2.91 ≈ 8.51
G² = 8.5094 ≈ 8.51
So A × H = G² (to the accuracy of the rounded values).
Answer: A = 2.925, H ≈ 2.91, G ≈ ±2.92, and A × H = G² is verified

Q: Q4(ii). Find the arithmetic, harmonic and geometric means of: -6 and -216. Also verify that A × H = G².

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2), H = (2ab)/(a + b), G = ±√(ab)
Here a = -6 and b = -216.
A = (-6 + (-216))/(2) = (-222)/(2) = -111
ab = (-6) × (-216) = 1296
G = ±√(1296) = ±36
H = (2 × 1296)/(-222) = (2592)/(-222) ≈ -11.68
Verification: A × H = (-111) × (-(432)/(37)) because H = -(2592)/(222) = -(432)/(37).
A × H = (111 × 432)/(37) = 1296
G² = (±36)² = 1296
So A × H = G².
Answer: A = -111, H ≈ -11.68, G = ±36, and A × H = G² is verified

Q: Q4(iii). Find the arithmetic, harmonic and geometric means of: x + y and x - y. Also verify that A × H = G².

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2), H = (2ab)/(a + b), G = ±√(ab)
Here a = x + y and b = x - y.
A = ((x + y) + (x - y))/(2) = (2x)/(2) = x
ab = (x + y)(x - y) = x² - y²
G = ±√(x² - y²)
H = (2(x² - y²))/((x + y) + (x - y)) = (2(x² - y²))/(2x) = (x² - y²)/(x)
Verification: A × H = x × (x² - y²)/(x) = x² - y²
G² = (±√(x² - y²))² = x² - y²
So A × H = G².
Answer: A = x, G = ±√(x² - y²), H = (x² - y²)/(x), and A × H = G² is verified

Q: Q5. For what value of n will (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) be the harmonic mean between a and b?

Ans: Formula: the harmonic mean between a and b is H = (2ab)/(a + b)
Set (aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) = (2ab)/(a + b)
Cross-multiplying: (a + b)(aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹) = 2ab(aⁿ + bⁿ)
aⁿ⁺² + abⁿ⁺¹ + aⁿ⁺¹b + bⁿ⁺² = 2aⁿ⁺¹b + 2abⁿ⁺¹
Simplifying: aⁿ⁺² + bⁿ⁺² = aⁿ⁺¹b + abⁿ⁺¹
aⁿ⁺² - aⁿ⁺¹b = abⁿ⁺¹ - bⁿ⁺²
aⁿ⁺¹(a - b) = bⁿ⁺¹(a - b)
Since a ≠ b, divide by (a - b): aⁿ⁺¹ = bⁿ⁺¹
This holds when n + 1 = 0.
n = -1
Check for n = -1: (a⁰ + b⁰)/((1)/(a) + (1)/(b)) = (2)/((a + b)/(ab)) = (2ab)/(a + b), which is the harmonic mean.
Answer: n = -1

Q: Q6. Insert two harmonic means between 12 and 48.

Ans: Formula: insert the corresponding arithmetic means between the reciprocals, using d = ((1)/(b) - (1)/(a))/(n + 1)
The reciprocals (1)/(12) and (1)/(48) are the extremes of an A.P. with 4 terms.
d = ((1)/(48) - (1)/(12))/(2 + 1)
(1)/(48) - (1)/(12) = (1)/(48) - (4)/(48) = -(3)/(48)
d = (-(3)/(48))/(3) = -(1)/(48)
First reciprocal mean = (1)/(12) - (1)/(48) = (4)/(48) - (1)/(48) = (3)/(48) = (1)/(16)
So the first harmonic mean is 16.
Second reciprocal mean = (1)/(16) - (1)/(48) = (3)/(48) - (1)/(48) = (2)/(48) = (1)/(24)
So the second harmonic mean is 24.
Answer: 16, 24

Q: Q7. Insert four harmonic means between (7)/(3) and (7)/(11).

Ans: Formula: insert the corresponding arithmetic means between the reciprocals, using d = ((1)/(b) - (1)/(a))/(n + 1)
The reciprocals (3)/(7) and (11)/(7) are the extremes of an A.P. with 6 terms.
d = ((11)/(7) - (3)/(7))/(4 + 1)
d = ((8)/(7))/(5) = (8)/(35)
First reciprocal mean = (3)/(7) + (8)/(35) = (15)/(35) + (8)/(35) = (23)/(35), so H₁ = (35)/(23)
Second reciprocal mean = (23)/(35) + (8)/(35) = (31)/(35), so H₂ = (35)/(31)
Third reciprocal mean = (31)/(35) + (8)/(35) = (39)/(35), so H₃ = (35)/(39)
Fourth reciprocal mean = (39)/(35) + (8)/(35) = (47)/(35), so H₄ = (35)/(47)
Answer: (35)/(23), (35)/(31), (35)/(39), (35)/(47)

Q: Q8. Prove that the square of the geometric mean of two numbers equals the product of the arithmetic mean and the harmonic mean of the two numbers.

Ans: Given: two numbers a and b
To Prove: G² = A × H
Formula: A = (a + b)/(2), H = (2ab)/(a + b), G = √(ab)
A × H = ((a + b)/(2)) × ((2ab)/(a + b))
The factors (a + b) and 2 cancel.
A × H = ab
G² = (√(ab))² = ab
So G² = A × H.
Hence proved.

Q: Q9. The arithmetic mean of two numbers is 8, and the harmonic mean is 6. What are the numbers?

Ans: Formula: G² = A × H, A = (a + b)/(2), and ab = G²
A = 8 gives a + b = 2 × 8 = 16.
H = 6 and A = 8 give G² = A × H = 8 × 6 = 48.
So ab = 48.
a and b are the roots of x² - (a + b)x + ab = 0.
x² - 16x + 48 = 0
(x - 4)(x - 12) = 0
x = 4 or x = 12
Answer: 4 and 12 (or 12 and 4)

Q: Q10. The harmonic mean of two numbers is 4(4)/(5) and the geometric mean is 6. What are the numbers?

Ans: Formula: G² = A × H, A = (a + b)/(2), and ab = G²
H = 4(4)/(5) = (24)/(5) and G = 6.
G² = 36.
A = (G²)/(H) = (36)/((24)/(5))
A = 36 × (5)/(24) = (15)/(2)
a + b = 2A = 2 × (15)/(2) = 15
ab = G² = 36
a and b are the roots of x² - (a + b)x + ab = 0.
x² - 15x + 36 = 0
(x - 3)(x - 12) = 0
x = 3 or x = 12
Answer: 3 and 12 (or 12 and 3)

mcqs.why: The reciprocals 2, 5, 8, ... form an A.P. with a₁ = 2, d = 3. Its 9th term = 2 + (9 - 1)(3) = 2 + 24 = 26. The H.P. term is the reciprocal: (1)/(26).

mcqs.q: The 20th term of the H.P. 6, 2, (6)/(5), ... is:
mcqs.why: The reciprocals (1)/(6), (1)/(2), (5)/(6), ... form an A.P. with d = (1)/(3). Its 20th term = (1)/(6) + 19 × (1)/(3) = (13)/(2). The H.P. term is the reciprocal: (2)/(13).

mcqs.q: An H.P. has 2nd term (1)/(2) and 5th term -(1)/(4). Its 12th term is:
mcqs.why: Reciprocals give an A.P. with a₁ + d = 2 and a₁ + 4d = -4. Subtracting: 3d = -6, d = -2, a₁ = 4. 12th A.P. term = 4 + 11 × (-2) = -18. The H.P. term is the reciprocal: -(1)/(18).

mcqs.q: The first of two harmonic means between 12 and 48 is:
mcqs.why: Reciprocals (1)/(12), (1)/(48) bound an A.P. with d = ((1)/(48) - (1)/(12))/(3) = -(1)/(48). First reciprocal mean = (1)/(12) - (1)/(48) = (1)/(16), so the harmonic mean is 16.

mcqs.q: Two numbers have A.M. 8 and H.M. 6. Their product is:
mcqs.why: Use G² = A × H and ab = G². G² = 8 × 6 = 48, so ab = 48. The numbers satisfy x² - 16x + 48 = 0, giving 4 and 12.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 4
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Interleaved series are summed by separating the two A.P.s; 1 + 4 + 6 + 5 + 11 + 6 + ... to 200 terms sums to 30200.
  • If a, b, c are in G.P., then a², b², c² are also in G.P.
  • For two positive numbers, G² = AH.
  • Four arithmetic means between 2 and -18 are -2, -6, -10, -14.
  • With a₁ = 8, d = -1: the general term is 9 - n, Sₙ = (n)/(2)(17 - n) and S₁₀ = 35.
  • The sum of natural numbers between 250 and 1000 divisible by 3 is 156375.
  • Three numbers in G.P. with sum 26 and product 216 are 2, 6, 18.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Choose the correct option. The sum to 200 terms of the series 1 + 4 + 6 + 5 + 11 + 6 + ...... is

Options: (a) 20,300 (b) 29,800 (c) 30,200 (d) None of these

Correct answer: 30,200

Q: Q1(ii). Choose the correct option. If the sum of the series 2 + 5 + 8 + 11 ...... is 60100, then the number of the terms is

Options: (a) 100 (b) 200 (c) 150 (d) 250

Correct answer: 200

Q: Q1(iii). Choose the correct option. If a, b, c are in G.P., then

Options: (a) a², b², c² are in G.P. (b) a²(b + c), c²(a + b), b²(a + c) are in G.P. (c) (a)/(b + c), (b)/(c + a), (c)/(a + b) are in G.P. (d) None of these

Correct answer: a², b², c² are in G.P.

Q: Q1(iv). Choose the correct option. If the nth term of an A.P is 4n + 1, then the common difference is:

Options: (a) 3 (b) 4 (c) 5 (d) 6

Correct answer: 4

Q: Q1(v). Choose the correct option. Which of the following is not a G.P.?

Options: (a) 2, 4, 8, 16, ........ (b) 5, 25, 125, 625, ...... (c) 1.5, 3.0, 6.0, 12.0 ..... (d) 8, 16, 24, 32, ..........

Correct answer: 8, 16, 24, 32, ..........

Q: Q1(vi). Choose the correct option. There are four arithmetic means between 2 and -18. The means are

Options: (a) -4, -7, -10, -13 (b) 1, -4, -7, -10 (c) -2, -5, -9, -13 (d) -2, -6, -10, -14

Correct answer: -2, -6, -10, -14

Q: Q1(vii). Choose the correct option. If A, G and H are A.M, G.M and H.M. of any two positive numbers, then find the relation between A, G and H.

Options: (a) A² = GH (b) G² = AH (c) H² = AG (d) G² = A²H

Correct answer: G² = AH

Q: Q1(viii). Choose the correct option. Find the number of terms to be added in the series 27, 9, 3, ...... so that the sum is 1093/27

Options: (a) 6 (b) 7 (c) 8 (d) 9

Correct answer: 7

Q: Q1(ix). Choose the correct option. Find the value of p (p > 0) if (15)/(4) + p, (5)/(2) + 2p and 2 + p are the three consecutive terms of a geometric progression

Options: (a) (3)/(4) (b) (1)/(4) (c) (5)/(3) (d) (1)/(2)

Correct answer: (1)/(4)

Q: Q1(x). Choose the correct option. The 10th term of harmonic progression 1/5, 4/19, 2/9, 4/17, ... is

Options: (a) 11/4 (b) 13/4 (c) 4/13 (d) 4/11

Correct answer: 4/11

Q: Q1(xi). Choose the correct option. Find the sum of 3 geometric means between 1/3 and 1/48 (r > 0).

Options: (a) 1/4 (b) 5/24 (c) 7/24 (d) 1/3

Correct answer: 7/24

Q: Q2(i). If the first term and common difference in an A.P are 8 and -1 respectively, then find: General term

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = 8 and d = -1.
aₙ = 8 + (n - 1)(-1)
aₙ = 8 - n + 1
aₙ = 9 - n
Answer: tₙ = 9 - n

Q: Q2(ii). If the first term and common difference in an A.P are 8 and -1 respectively, then find: The Progression

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d, with a₁ = 8 and d = -1
First term = 8
Second term = 8 + (-1) = 7
Third term = 7 + (-1) = 6
Fourth term = 6 + (-1) = 5
Answer: The progression is 8, 7, 6, 5, ...

Q: Q2(iii). If the first term and common difference in an A.P are 8 and -1 respectively, then find: The 10th term

Ans: Formula: aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
Here a₁ = 8, d = -1 and n = 10.
a₁₀ = 8 + (10 - 1)(-1)
a₁₀ = 8 + (9)(-1)
a₁₀ = 8 - 9
a₁₀ = -1
Answer: t₁₀ = -1

Q: Q2(iv). If the first term and common difference in an A.P are 8 and -1 respectively, then find: The expression for sum to n terms and hence sum to 10 terms.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
Here a₁ = 8 and d = -1.
Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2(8) + (n - 1)(-1)]
Sₙ = (n)/(2)[16 - n + 1]
Sₙ = (n)/(2)(17 - n)
For n = 10: S₁₀ = (10)/(2)(17 - 10)
S₁₀ = 5 × 7
S₁₀ = 35
Answer: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(17 - n), S₁₀ = 35

Q: Q3. If the sum of the n terms of the series 54, 51, 48, .... is 513, then find the value of n.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
Here a₁ = 54 and d = 51 - 54 = -3.
513 = (n)/(2)[2(54) + (n - 1)(-3)]
513 = (n)/(2)[108 - 3n + 3]
513 = (n)/(2)(111 - 3n)
Multiply both sides by 2: 1026 = n(111 - 3n)
1026 = 111n - 3n²
3n² - 111n + 1026 = 0
Divide by 3: n² - 37n + 342 = 0
(n - 18)(n - 19) = 0
n = 18 or n = 19
Both values are valid because the terms around them cancel in pairs (the 19th term is 0).
Answer: n = 18 or 19

Q: Q4. If the sum of n terms of an A.P. is 2n + 3n², generate the progression and find the nth term

Ans: Formula: aₙ = Sₙ - Sₙ₋₁
Given: Sₙ = 2n + 3n²
Sₙ₋₁ = 2(n - 1) + 3(n - 1)²
= 2n - 2 + 3(n² - 2n + 1)
= 2n - 2 + 3n² - 6n + 3
= 3n² - 4n + 1
aₙ = (2n + 3n²) - (3n² - 4n + 1)
aₙ = 6n - 1
Check the first terms: a₁ = 6(1) - 1 = 5, a₂ = 6(2) - 1 = 11, a₃ = 6(3) - 1 = 17.
Answer: The progression is 5, 11, 17, ... and the nth term is 6n - 1

Q: Q5. Find the sum of all natural numbers between 250 and 1000 which are exactly divisible by 3.

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)(a₁ + aₙ) and aₙ = a₁ + (n - 1)d
The numbers are 252, 255, 258, ..., 999, an A.P. with a₁ = 252, d = 3, aₙ = 999.
999 = 252 + (n - 1)(3)
747 = (n - 1)(3)
n - 1 = (747)/(3) = 249
n = 250
S₂₅₀ = (250)/(2)(252 + 999)
S₂₅₀ = 125 × 1251
S₂₅₀ = 156375
Answer: 156375

Q: Q6. Find the sum of the series 1, 2/5, 4/25, 8/125, ........., ∞

Ans: Formula: S = (a₁)/(1 - r) for |r| < 1 (sum of an infinite geometric series)
Here a₁ = 1.
r = ((2)/(5))/(1) = (2)/(5)
|r| = (2)/(5) < 1, so the infinite sum exists.
S = (1)/(1 - (2)/(5))
S = (1)/((3)/(5))
S = (5)/(3)
Answer: (5)/(3)

Q: Q7. If a, b, c are in A.P. and x, y, z are in G.P, show that xᵇ yᶜ zᵃ = xᶜ yᵃ zᵇ

Ans: Given: a, b, c are in A.P. and x, y, z are in G.P.
To Prove: xᵇ yᶜ zᵃ = xᶜ yᵃ zᵇ
Since a, b, c are in A.P., 2b = a + c, so b - c = a - b and c - a = 2(a - b) with signs as used below.
Since x, y, z are in G.P., y² = xz, so 2 log y = log x + log z.
Take log of the left side: b log x + c log y + a log z
Take log of the right side: c log x + a log y + b log z
Difference (left - right) = (b - c) log x + (c - a) log y + (a - b) log z
From the A.P., b - c = -(c - b) and using b = (a + c)/(2): b - c = (a - c)/(2) and a - b = (a - c)/(2), while c - a = -(a - c).
Difference = ((a - c)/(2)) log x - (a - c) log y + ((a - c)/(2)) log z
= ((a - c)/(2))(log x + log z - 2 log y)
= ((a - c)/(2))(log(xz) - log(y²))
Since y² = xz, log(xz) - log(y²) = 0.
So the difference is 0, the two logs are equal, and the two sides are equal.
Hence proved.

Q: Q8. Find the arithmetic mean between 10(1)/(2) and 25(1)/(2).

Ans: Formula: A = (a + b)/(2)
Here a = 10(1)/(2) = (21)/(2) and b = 25(1)/(2) = (51)/(2).
A = (((21)/(2) + (51)/(2)))/(2)
A = (((72)/(2)))/(2)
A = (36)/(2)
A = 18
Answer: 18

Q: Q9. Find three numbers of a G.P. whose sum is 26 and product is 216.

Ans: Formula: for three numbers in G.P. take them as (a)/(r), a, ar; their product is a³
Product: ((a)/(r)) × a × (ar) = 216
a³ = 216
a = 6, since 6³ = 216.
Sum: (6)/(r) + 6 + 6r = 26
(6)/(r) + 6r = 26 - 6 = 20
Divide by 2: (3)/(r) + 3r = 10
Multiply by r: 3 + 3r² = 10r
3r² - 10r + 3 = 0
(3r - 1)(r - 3) = 0
r = 3 or r = (1)/(3)
For r = 3: the numbers are 6/3, 6, 6 × 3 = 2, 6, 18.
For r = (1)/(3): the numbers are 18, 6, 2.
Answer: 2, 6 and 18 (or 18, 6 and 2)

Q: Q10. How many odd integers beginning with 15 must be taken for their sum to be equal to 975?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (n)/(2)[2a₁ + (n - 1)d]
The odd integers 15, 17, 19, ... form an A.P. with a₁ = 15 and d = 2.
975 = (n)/(2)[2(15) + (n - 1)(2)]
975 = (n)/(2)[30 + 2n - 2]
975 = (n)/(2)(2n + 28)
975 = n(n + 14)
n² + 14n - 975 = 0
(n + 39)(n - 25) = 0
n = 25 (rejecting the negative value n = -39)
Answer: 25

Q: Q11. A gas-filled balloon has risen 100 feet. In each succeeding minute, the balloon rises only 50% as far as it rose in the previous minute. How far will it rise in 5 minutes?

Ans: Formula: Sₙ = (a₁(1 - rⁿ))/(1 - r) for |r| < 1
The balloon has already risen 100 feet in the first minute.
In each succeeding minute it rises 50% of the previous minute's rise, so the rises form a G.P. with r = (1)/(2).
Rises in the next 5 minutes: 50, 25, (25)/(2), (25)/(4), (25)/(8) feet.
Sum of these 5 rises = (50(1 - ((1)/(2))⁵))/(1 - (1)/(2))
= (50(1 - (1)/(32)))/((1)/(2))
= 100 × (31)/(32)
= (775)/(8) = 96.875 feet
Total rise = 100 + 96.875
= 196.875 feet
Answer: 196.875 feet

mcqs.q: The sum to 200 terms of the series 1 + 4 + 6 + 5 + 11 + 6 + ... is:
If the sum of the series 2 + 5 + 8 + 11 + ... is 60100, then the number of terms is:
If a, b, c are in G.P., then:
options: a², b², c² are in G.P.
a²(b + c), c²(a + b), b²(a + c) are in G.P.
(a)/(b + c), (b)/(c + a), (c)/(a + b) are in G.P.
a, b, c are in A.P.
mcqs.why: If b = ar and c = ar², then a², b², c² are a², a²r², a²r⁴, which form a G.P. with common ratio r². Hence a², b², c² are in G.P.

mcqs.q: If the nth term of an A.P. is 4n + 1, then the common difference is:
mcqs.why: aₙ₊₁ - aₙ = [4(n + 1) + 1] - [4n + 1] = (4n + 5) - (4n + 1) = 4. So the common difference is 4.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is not a G.P.?
mcqs.why: Check ratios: 8, 16, 24, 32 has ratios (16)/(8) = 2 but (24)/(16) = (3)/(2), which differ, so it is not a G.P. (it is an A.P. with d = 8). The others have constant ratios 2, 5 and 2.

mcqs.q: There are four arithmetic means between 2 and -18. The means are:
If A, G and H are the A.M., G.M. and H.M. of two positive numbers, then:
mcqs.why: Use A = (a + b)/(2), H = (2ab)/(a + b), G² = ab. A × H = ((a + b)/(2)) × ((2ab)/(a + b)) = ab = G². Hence G² = AH.

mcqs.q: The number of terms of 27, 9, 3, ... needed for the sum (1093)/(27) is:
Find p (p > 0) if (15)/(4) + p, (5)/(2) + 2p, 2 + p are consecutive terms of a G.P.:
mcqs.why: For a G.P., ((5)/(2) + 2p)² = ((15)/(4) + p)(2 + p). Expanding gives 12p² + 17p - 5 = 0 after multiplying by 4; discriminant = 529 = 23², so p = (-17 + 23)/(24) = (1)/(4).

mcqs.q: The 10th term of the harmonic progression (1)/(5), (4)/(19), (2)/(9), (4)/(17), ... is:
mcqs.why: Reciprocals are 5, (19)/(4), (9)/(2), (17)/(4), ..., an A.P. with d = -(1)/(4). 10th reciprocal = 5 + 9 × (-(1)/(4)) = (11)/(4). The H.P. term is the reciprocal: (4)/(11).

mcqs.q: The sum of 3 geometric means between (1)/(3) and (1)/(48) (r > 0) is:
If a₁ = 8 and d = -1 in an A.P., the general term is:

The sum of all natural numbers between 250 and 1000 divisible by 3 is:
Three numbers in G.P. have sum 26 and product 216. The middle number is:
mcqs.why: Take the numbers as (a)/(r), a, ar. Product: a³ = 216, so a = 6, the middle number. Check: (6)/(r) + 6r = 20 gives r = 3 or (1)/(3), numbers 2, 6, 18.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Standard sums: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]².
  • 1² + 3² + 5² + ... to n terms = (n(4n² - 1))/(3); up to 99² the sum is 166650.
  • 2² + 4² + 6² + ... to n terms = (2n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(3).
  • 1³ + 3³ + 5³ + ... to n terms = n²(2n² - 1).
  • 1·2 + 2·3 + ... + 99·100 = 333300.
  • 1·2·3 + 2·3·4 + ... to n terms = (n(n + 1)(n + 2)(n + 3))/(4).

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Sum the following series up to n terms: 1² + 3² + 5² + 7² + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = (2k − 1)² = 4k² − 4k + 1
Sₙ = Σ(4k² − 4k + 1) = 4Σk² − 4Σk + Σ1
Sₙ = 4 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) − 4 × (n(n + 1))/(2) + n
Sₙ = (2n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(3) − 2n(n + 1) + n
Take n common: Sₙ = n[(2(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(3) − 2(n + 1) + 1]
Sₙ = n[(4n² + 6n + 2 − 6n − 6 + 3)/(3)]
Answer: Sₙ = (n(4n² − 1))/(3)

Q: Q1(ii). Sum the following series up to n terms: 1² + (1² + 2²) + (1² + 2² + 3²) + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth bracket is 1² + 2² + ... + k² = (k(k + 1)(2k + 1))/(6)
So Tₖ = (k(k + 1)(2k + 1))/(6) = (2k³ + 3k² + k)/(6)
Sₙ = (1)/(6)[2Σk³ + 3Σk² + Σk]
Sₙ = (1)/(6)[2 × (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) + 3 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + (n(n + 1))/(2)]
Sₙ = (n(n + 1))/(6) × [(n(n + 1))/(2) + (2n + 1)/(2) + (1)/(2)]
Sₙ = (n(n + 1))/(6) × [(n² + n + 2n + 2)/(2)]
Sₙ = (n(n + 1))/(6) × [(n + 1)(n + 2)/(2)]
Answer: Sₙ = (n(n + 1)²(n + 2))/(12)

Q: Q1(iii). Sum the following series up to n terms: 2² + 4² + 6² + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = (2k)² = 4k²
Sₙ = Σ4k² = 4Σk²
Sₙ = 4 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6)
Answer: Sₙ = (2n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(3)

Q: Q1(iv). Sum the following series up to n terms: 1³ + 3³ + 5³ + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = (2k − 1)³ = 8k³ − 12k² + 6k − 1
Sₙ = Σ(8k³ − 12k² + 6k − 1) = 8Σk³ − 12Σk² + 6Σk − Σ1
Sₙ = 8 × (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) − 12 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + 6 × (n(n + 1))/(2) − n
Sₙ = 2n²(n + 1)² − 2n(n + 1)(2n + 1) + 3n(n + 1) − n
Expand: Sₙ = (2n⁴ + 4n³ + 2n²) − (4n³ + 6n² + 2n) + (3n² + 3n) − n
Sₙ = 2n⁴ − n²
Answer: Sₙ = n(2n³ − n) = n²(2n² − 1)

Q: Q1(v). Sum the following series up to n terms: 1³ + 5³ + 9³ + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = (4k − 3)³ = 64k³ − 144k² + 108k − 27
Sₙ = Σ(64k³ − 144k² + 108k − 27) = 64Σk³ − 144Σk² + 108Σk − 27Σ1
Sₙ = 64 × (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) − 144 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + 108 × (n(n + 1))/(2) − 27n
Sₙ = 16n²(n + 1)² − 24n(n + 1)(2n + 1) + 54n(n + 1) − 27n
Take n common and simplify the bracket:
16n(n + 1)² = 16n³ + 32n² + 16n
−24(n + 1)(2n + 1) = −48n² − 72n − 24
54(n + 1) − 27 = 54n + 27
Bracket total: 16n³ − 16n² − 2n + 3
Answer: Sₙ = n(16n³ − 16n² − 2n + 3)

Q: Q2. Find the sum 1·2 + 2·3 + 3·4 + ... + 99·100

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = k(k + 1) = k² + k
Sum to 99 terms: S = Σk² + Σk with n = 99
S = (99 × 100 × 199)/(6) + (99 × 100)/(2)
S = 328350 + 4950
S = 333300
Answer: 333300 (= 33 × 100 × 101)

Q: Q3. Find the sum 1² + 3² + 5² + 7² + ... + 99²

Ans: Formula: The sum of the squares of the first n odd numbers is (n(4n² − 1))/(3).
99 is the 50th odd number, so n = 50
S = (50 × (4 × 50² − 1))/(3)
S = (50 × 9999)/(3)
S = 50 × 3333
Answer: 166650

Q: Q4. Find the sum 2 + (2 + 5) + (2 + 5 + 8) + ... to n terms

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth bracket is the sum of k terms of the A.P. 2, 5, 8, ...
Tₖ = (k)/(2)[2 × 2 + (k − 1) × 3] = (k(3k + 1))/(2) = (3k² + k)/(2)
Sₙ = (1)/(2)[3Σk² + Σk]
Sₙ = (1)/(2)[3 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + (n(n + 1))/(2)]
Sₙ = (1)/(2) × (n(n + 1))/(2) × [(2n + 1) + 1]
Sₙ = (n(n + 1)(2n + 2))/(4)
Answer: Sₙ = (n(n + 1)²)/(2)

Q: Q5. Sum 2 + 5 + 10 + 17 + ... to n terms

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
Compare with the squares: 2 = 1² + 1, 5 = 2² + 1, 10 = 3² + 1, 17 = 4² + 1
The kth term is Tₖ = k² + 1
Sₙ = Σk² + Σ1 = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + n
Sₙ = n[(n + 1)(2n + 1) + 6]/(6)
Sₙ = n[2n² + 3n + 1 + 6]/(6)
Answer: Sₙ = (n(2n² + 3n + 7))/(6)

Q: Q6. Sum to n terms: 1·2·3 + 2·3·4 + 3·4·5 + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = k(k + 1)(k + 2) = k³ + 3k² + 2k
Sₙ = Σk³ + 3Σk² + 2Σk
Sₙ = (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) + 3 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + 2 × (n(n + 1))/(2)
Take n(n + 1) common: Sₙ = n(n + 1)[(n(n + 1))/(4) + (2n + 1)/(2) + 1]
Sₙ = n(n + 1)[(n² + n + 4n + 2 + 4)/(4)]
Sₙ = n(n + 1)(n² + 5n + 6)/(4)
Answer: Sₙ = (n(n + 1)(n + 2)(n + 3))/(4)
Note: The book's printed answer ((n(n + 1)(2n + 1)(n + 3))/(4)) is incorrect; the correct answer is (n(n + 1)(n + 2)(n + 3))/(4).

Q: Q7. Sum to n terms: 1·5·9 + 2·6·10 + 3·7·11 + ...

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = k(k + 4)(k + 8) = k³ + 12k² + 32k
Sₙ = Σk³ + 12Σk² + 32Σk
Sₙ = (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) + 12 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) + 32 × (n(n + 1))/(2)
Take n(n + 1) common: Sₙ = n(n + 1)[(n(n + 1))/(4) + 2(2n + 1) + 16]
Sₙ = n(n + 1)[(n² + n + 16n + 72)/(4)]
Sₙ = n(n + 1)(n² + 17n + 72)/(4)
Answer: Sₙ = (n(n + 1)(n + 8)(n + 9))/(4)

Q: Q8. Find the sum to 2n terms of the series whose nth term is 4n² + 5n + 1

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = 4k² + 5k + 1; sum from k = 1 to 2n.
Σk² (to 2n) = (2n(2n + 1)(4n + 1))/(6), Σk (to 2n) = (2n(2n + 1))/(2) = n(2n + 1), Σ1 (to 2n) = 2n
S = 4 × (n(2n + 1)(4n + 1))/(3) + 5n(2n + 1) + 2n
4Σk² = 4 × (2n(2n + 1)(4n + 1))/(6) = (4n(2n + 1)(4n + 1))/(3)
(2n + 1)(4n + 1) = 8n² + 6n + 1, so 4Σk² = (32n³ + 24n² + 4n)/(3)
5Σk + Σ1 = 5n(2n + 1) + 2n = 10n² + 7n = (30n² + 21n)/(3)
S = (32n³ + 24n² + 4n + 30n² + 21n)/(3)
S = (32n³ + 54n² + 25n)/(3)
Answer: S = (n(32n² + 54n + 25))/(3)

Q: Q9(i). Find the sum of n terms of the series whose nth term is n²(2n + 3)

Ans: Formulas used: Σk = (n(n + 1))/(2), Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², where each sum runs from k = 1 to n.
The kth term is Tₖ = k²(2k + 3) = 2k³ + 3k²
Sₙ = 2Σk³ + 3Σk²
Sₙ = 2 × (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) + 3 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6)
Take n(n + 1) common: Sₙ = n(n + 1)[(n(n + 1))/(2) + (2n + 1)/(2)]
Sₙ = n(n + 1)(n² + n + 2n + 1)/(2)
Answer: Sₙ = (n(n + 1)(n² + 3n + 1))/(2)

Q: Q9(ii). Find the sum of n terms of the series whose nth term is 3(4ⁿ + 2n²) − 4n³

Ans: Formulas used: Σk² = (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6), Σk³ = [(n(n + 1))/(2)]², and the G.P. sum Σ4ᵏ = (4(4ⁿ − 1))/(3).
The kth term is Tₖ = 3·4ᵏ + 6k² − 4k³
Sₙ = 3Σ4ᵏ + 6Σk² − 4Σk³
3Σ4ᵏ = 3 × (4(4ⁿ − 1))/(3) = 4ⁿ⁺¹ − 4
6Σk² = 6 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)
4Σk³ = 4 × (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) = n²(n + 1)²
Polynomial part: n(n + 1)(2n + 1) − n²(n + 1)² = n(n + 1)[(2n + 1) − n(n + 1)] = n(n + 1)(−n² + n + 1) = −n(n + 1)(n² − n − 1)
Answer: Sₙ = 4ⁿ⁺¹ − 4 − n(n + 1)(n² − n − 1)

mcqs.q: The sum 1² + 3² + 5² + ... to n terms is:
mcqs.why: The kth term is (2k - 1)² = 4k² - 4k + 1. Sₙ = 4Σk² - 4Σk + Σ1 = 4 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) - 4 × (n(n + 1))/(2) + n, which simplifies to (n(4n² - 1))/(3).

mcqs.q: The sum 1² + 3² + 5² + ... + 99² is:
The sum 2² + 4² + 6² + ... to n terms is:
The sum 1³ + 3³ + 5³ + ... to n terms is:
mcqs.why: The kth term is (2k - 1)³ = 8k³ - 12k² + 6k - 1. Sₙ = 8Σk³ - 12Σk² + 6Σk - Σ1, which expands and simplifies to 2n⁴ - n² = n²(2n² - 1).

mcqs.q: The series 2 + 5 + 10 + 17 + ... (nth term k² + 1) sums to n terms as:
The sum 1·2·3 + 2·3·4 + 3·4·5 + ... to n terms is:
The sum 1·5·9 + 2·6·10 + 3·7·11 + ... to n terms is:
The sum to 2n terms of the series with nth term 4n² + 5n + 1 is:
The sum of n terms of the series with nth term n²(2n + 3) is:
mcqs.why: Tₖ = 2k³ + 3k², so Sₙ = 2Σk³ + 3Σk² = 2 × (n²(n + 1)²)/(4) + 3 × (n(n + 1)(2n + 1))/(6) = n(n + 1)(n² + 3n + 1)/(2) after taking n(n + 1) common.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Arithmetico-geometric method: multiply Sₙ by the ratio r and subtract to reduce to a G.P.
  • 1·2 + 2·2² + 3·2³ + ... to n terms = 2 + (n - 1)2ⁿ⁺¹.
  • Sum to infinity: S∞ = (a)/(1 - r) + (dr)/((1 - r)²) for |r| < 1.
  • 1 + (4)/(3) + (9)/(3²) + (16)/(3³) + ... to infinity = (9)/(2), using Σk²rᵏ⁻¹ = (1 + r)/((1 - r)³).
  • The nth term of (0)/(1) + (1)/(2) + (2)/(4) + (3)/(8) + ... is (n - 1)/(2ⁿ⁻¹).
  • 5 + (7)/(3) + 1 + (11)/(27) + ... to infinity = 9, and 3 + 5r + 7r² + ... = (44)/(9) gives r = (1)/(4).

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Sum to n terms the following series: 1·2 + 2·2² + 3·2³ + 4·2⁴ + ...

Ans: Method: Multiply by the ratio 2 and subtract (arithmetico-geometric method).
Let Sₙ = 1·2 + 2·2² + 3·2³ + ... + n·2ⁿ ... (1)
2Sₙ = 1·2² + 2·2³ + ... + (n − 1)·2ⁿ + n·2ⁿ⁺¹ ... (2)
Subtract (2) from (1): −Sₙ = (2 + 2² + 2³ + ... + 2ⁿ) − n·2ⁿ⁺¹
The bracket is a G.P.: 2 + 2² + ... + 2ⁿ = (2(2ⁿ − 1))/(2 − 1) = 2ⁿ⁺¹ − 2
−Sₙ = 2ⁿ⁺¹ − 2 − n·2ⁿ⁺¹
Sₙ = n·2ⁿ⁺¹ − 2ⁿ⁺¹ + 2
Answer: Sₙ = 2 + (n − 1)2ⁿ⁺¹

Q: Q1(ii). Sum to n terms the following series: 1 + 4x + 7x² + 10x³ + ...

Ans: Formula (arithmetico-geometric sum): Sₙ = (a)/(1 − r) + (dr(1 − rⁿ⁻¹))/((1 − r)²) − ([a + (n − 1)d]rⁿ)/(1 − r), where a is the first A.P. term, d its common difference and r the G.P. ratio.
Here the A.P. is 1, 4, 7, 10, ... so a = 1, d = 3, and the G.P. ratio is r = x.
Sₙ = (1)/(1 − x) + (3x(1 − xⁿ⁻¹))/((1 − x)²) − ((3n − 2)xⁿ)/(1 − x)
Combine the first and last terms over (1 − x):
Answer: Sₙ = (1 − (3n − 2)xⁿ)/(1 − x) + (3x(1 − xⁿ⁻¹))/((1 − x)²)

Q: Q1(iii). Sum to n terms the following series: 1 + 2x + 3x² + 4x³ + ...

Ans: Method: Multiply by the ratio x and subtract (arithmetico-geometric method).
Let Sₙ = 1 + 2x + 3x² + ... + nxⁿ⁻¹ ... (1)
xSₙ = x + 2x² + ... + (n − 1)xⁿ⁻¹ + nxⁿ ... (2)
Subtract (2) from (1): (1 − x)Sₙ = 1 + x + x² + ... + xⁿ⁻¹ − nxⁿ
The bracket is a G.P.: 1 + x + ... + xⁿ⁻¹ = (1 − xⁿ)/(1 − x)
(1 − x)Sₙ = (1 − xⁿ)/(1 − x) − nxⁿ
Answer: Sₙ = (1 − xⁿ)/((1 − x)²) − (nxⁿ)/(1 − x)

Q: Q1(iv). Sum to n terms the following series: 1 + (3)/(2) + (5)/(4) + (7)/(8) + ...

Ans: Formula (arithmetico-geometric sum): Sₙ = (a)/(1 − r) + (dr(1 − rⁿ⁻¹))/((1 − r)²) − ([a + (n − 1)d]rⁿ)/(1 − r), where a is the first A.P. term, d its common difference and r the G.P. ratio.
Here the A.P. is 1, 3, 5, 7, ... so a = 1, d = 2, and the G.P. ratio is r = (1)/(2).
(a)/(1 − r) = (1)/(1 − (1)/(2)) = 2
(dr)/((1 − r)²) = (2 × (1)/(2))/((1)/(2))² = 4, and rⁿ⁻¹ = (1)/(2ⁿ⁻¹)
[a + (n − 1)d] = 2n − 1 and rⁿ = (1)/(2ⁿ)
Substitute these values in the formula and simplify:
Answer: Sₙ = 2 + 4(1 − (1)/(2ⁿ⁻¹)) − (2n − 1)/(2ⁿ⁻¹)

Q: Q1(v). Sum to n terms the following series: 1 − 7x + 13x² − 19x³ + ...

Ans: Formula (arithmetico-geometric sum): Sₙ = (a)/(1 − r) + (dr(1 − rⁿ⁻¹))/((1 − r)²) − ([a + (n − 1)d]rⁿ)/(1 − r), where a is the first A.P. term, d its common difference and r the G.P. ratio.
Write the series as 1 + 7(−x) + 13(−x)² + 19(−x)³ + ...; the A.P. is 1, 7, 13, 19, ... so a = 1, d = 6, and r = −x.
Sₙ = (1)/(1 + x) + (6(−x)(1 − (−x)ⁿ⁻¹))/((1 + x)²) − ((6n − 5)(−x)ⁿ)/(1 + x)
Combine the first and last terms over (1 + x):
Answer: Sₙ = (1 − (6n − 5)(−x)ⁿ)/(1 + x) − (6x[1 − (−x)ⁿ⁻¹])/((1 + x)²)

Q: Q2(i). Find the sum to infinity of the following series: 1² + 3²x + 5²x² + 7²x³ + ..., x < 1

Ans: Method: Split (2k − 1)² = 4k² − 4k + 1 and use Σk²xᵏ⁻¹ = (1 + x)/((1 − x)³), Σkxᵏ⁻¹ = (1)/((1 − x)²), Σxᵏ⁻¹ = (1)/(1 − x) for |x| < 1.
S∞ = Σ(4k² − 4k + 1)xᵏ⁻¹ = 4Σk²xᵏ⁻¹ − 4Σkxᵏ⁻¹ + Σxᵏ⁻¹
S∞ = (4(1 + x))/((1 − x)³) − (4)/((1 − x)²) + (1)/(1 − x)
Put over the common denominator (1 − x)³:
Numerator: 4(1 + x) − 4(1 − x) + (1 − x)² = 4 + 4x − 4 + 4x + 1 − 2x + x² = 1 + 6x + x²
S∞ = (1 + 6x + x²)/((1 − x)³)
Regrouped as in the book's answer key:
Answer: S∞ = (1 + 7x)/((1 − x)²) + (8x²)/((1 − x)³)

Q: Q2(ii). Find the sum to infinity of the following series: 1 + (4)/(3) + (9)/(3²) + (16)/(3³) + (25)/(3⁴) + ...

Ans: Formula: For |r| < 1, Σk²rᵏ⁻¹ = (1 + r)/((1 − r)³).
The kth term is (k²)/(3ᵏ⁻¹), so r = (1)/(3).
S∞ = (1 + (1)/(3))/((1 − (1)/(3))³)
S∞ = ((4)/(3))/((2)/(3))³
S∞ = ((4)/(3))/((8)/(27))
S∞ = (4)/(3) × (27)/(8)
Answer: S∞ = (9)/(2)

Q: Q3. Find the nth term of the following arithmetico-geometric series: (0)/(1) + (1)/(2) + (2)/(4) + (3)/(8) + (4)/(16) + (5)/(32) + ...

Ans: Rule: In an arithmetico-geometric series the nth term is [a + (n − 1)d] × rⁿ⁻¹.
The numerators 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, ... form an A.P. with a = 0 and d = 1.
The denominators 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, ... form a G.P. with ratio r = (1)/(2).
Tₙ = [0 + (n − 1)(1)] × ((1)/(2))ⁿ⁻¹
Answer: Tₙ = (n − 1)/(2ⁿ⁻¹)
Note: The book's printed answer (n2ⁿ⁻¹) is incorrect; the correct nth term is (n − 1)/(2ⁿ⁻¹).

Q: Q4. Find the sum of the following arithmetico-geometric series: 5 + (7)/(3) + 1 + (11)/(27) + ...

Ans: Formula: Sum to infinity of an arithmetico-geometric series, S∞ = (a)/(1 − r) + (dr)/((1 − r)²), valid for |r| < 1.
Write the series as (5)/(1) + (7)/(3) + (9)/(9) + (11)/(27) + ...
The numerators 5, 7, 9, 11, ... form an A.P. with a = 5, d = 2; the denominators give r = (1)/(3).
S∞ = (5)/(1 − (1)/(3)) + (2 × (1)/(3))/((1 − (1)/(3))²)
S∞ = (5)/((2)/(3)) + ((2)/(3))/((4)/(9))
S∞ = (15)/(2) + (3)/(2)
Answer: S∞ = 9

Q: Q5. If the sum to infinity of the series 3 + 5r + 7r² + ...... ∞ is (44)/(9), find the value of r.

Ans: Formula: S∞ = (a)/(1 − r) + (dr)/((1 − r)²) for an arithmetico-geometric series with |r| < 1.
Here a = 3 and d = 5 − 3 = 2.
(3)/(1 − r) + (2r)/((1 − r)²) = (44)/(9)
Multiply both sides by 9(1 − r)²: 27(1 − r) + 18r = 44(1 − r)²
27 − 27r + 18r = 44(1 − 2r + r²)
27 − 9r = 44 − 88r + 44r²
44r² − 79r + 17 = 0
Factor: (4r − 1)(11r − 17) = 0
r = (1)/(4) or r = (17)/(11)
r = (17)/(11) is rejected because |r| must be less than 1 for the sum to infinity to exist.
Answer: r = (1)/(4)
