lessons.title: Review Exercise 10
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • cos50°50′ cos9°10′ − sin50°50′ sin9°10′ = cos60° = (1)/(2) by cos(α + β).
  • If tan15° = 2 − √3 then cot75° = tan15°, so cot²75° = (2 − √3)² = 7 − 4√3.
  • tan(α + β) = (1)/(2) and tan α = (1)/(3) give tan β = (1)/(7).
  • sin θ cos(90° − θ) + cos θ sin(90° − θ) = sin²θ + cos²θ = 1.
  • (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sin θ) = cos θ, since sec θ + tan θ = (1 + sin θ)/(cos θ).
  • sin(x − (π)/(2)) = −cos x; a unit-circle point in Quadrant III with x-coordinate −(4)/(5) has y-coordinate −(3)/(5).
  • sin a cos a = (1)/(2) sin(2a) is an identity; the other listed equations are not.
  • (2sinθ sin2θ)/(cos θ + cos3θ) = tan2θ tanθ and cos4θ = 1 − 8sin²θ cos²θ.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). cos50°50′ cos9°10′ − sin50°50′ sin9°10′ = ?

Options: (a) 0 (b) (1)/(2) (c) 1 (d) (√3)/(2)

Correct answer: (1)/(2)

Q: Q1(ii). If tan15° = 2 − √3, then cot²75° = ?

Options: (a) 7 + √3 (b) 7 − 2√3 (c) 7 − 4√3 (d) 7 + 4√3

Correct answer: 7 − 4√3

Q: Q1(iii). If tan(α + β) = (1)/(2) and tan α = (1)/(3), then tan β = ?

Options: (a) (1)/(6) (b) (1)/(7) (c) 1 (d) (7)/(6)

Correct answer: (1)/(7)

Q: Q1(iv). sin θ cos(90° − θ) + cos θ sin(90° − θ) = ?

Options: (a) −1 (b) 2 (c) 0 (d) 1

Correct answer: 1

Q: Q1(v). (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sin θ) = ?

Options: (a) sin²θ (b) cos²θ (c) tan²θ (d) cos θ

Correct answer: cos θ

Q: Q1(vi). sin(x − (π)/(2)) = ?

Options: (a) sin x (b) −sin x (c) cos x (d) −cos x

Correct answer: −cos x

Q: Q1(vii). A point on the unit circle is in the third quadrant. If the x-coordinate of the point is −(4)/(5), then its y-coordinate is:

Options: (a) (3)/(5) (b) −(3)/(5) (c) −(2)/(5) (d) (5)/(3)

Correct answer: −(3)/(5)

Q: Q1(viii). Which of the following is an identity?

Options: (a) sin(a) cos(a) = (1)/(2) sin(2a) (b) sin a + cos a = 1 (c) sin(−a) = sin a (d) tan a = (cos a)/(sin a)

Correct answer: sin(a) cos(a) = (1)/(2) sin(2a)

Q: Q2. Prove that: (2sinθ sin2θ)/(cos θ + cos3θ) = tan2θ tanθ

Ans: Identities used: cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/(2)) cos((C − D)/(2)).
Denominator: cos θ + cos3θ = 2 cos((θ + 3θ)/(2)) cos((3θ − θ)/(2)) = 2 cos2θ cos θ
L.H.S = (2 sin θ sin2θ)/(2 cos2θ cos θ)
= ((sin2θ)/(cos2θ)) × ((sin θ)/(cos θ)) [rearranging the factors]
= tan2θ × tanθ
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q3. Prove that: (sin10a − sin4a)/(sin4a + sin2a) = (cos7a)/(cos a)

Ans: Identities used: sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/(2)) sin((C − D)/(2)) and sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D)/(2)) cos((C − D)/(2)).
Numerator: sin10a − sin4a = 2 cos((10a + 4a)/(2)) sin((10a − 4a)/(2)) = 2 cos7a sin3a
Denominator: sin4a + sin2a = 2 sin((4a + 2a)/(2)) cos((4a − 2a)/(2)) = 2 sin3a cos a
L.H.S = (2 cos7a sin3a)/(2 sin3a cos a)
= (cos7a)/(cos a) [cancelling 2 sin3a]
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q4. Prove that: sin²(θ/2) = (sin θ tan(θ/2))/(2)

Ans: Method: work from the right side using sin θ = 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2).
R.H.S = (sin θ tan(θ/2))/(2)
= (1)/(2) × sin θ × (sin(θ/2))/(cos(θ/2))
= (1)/(2) × 2 sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2) × (sin(θ/2))/(cos(θ/2)) [replacing sin θ]
= sin(θ/2) × sin(θ/2) [cancelling 2 and cos(θ/2)]
= sin²(θ/2)
= L.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q5. Prove that: tan θ · tan(θ/2) = sec θ − 1

Ans: Method: use the half-angle identity tan(θ/2) = (sin θ)/(1 + cos θ) and sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ.
L.H.S = tan θ · tan(θ/2)
= tan θ × (sin θ)/(1 + cos θ) [by the half-angle identity]
= (sin θ)/(cos θ) × (sin θ)/(1 + cos θ) [writing tan θ = (sin θ)/(cos θ)]
= (sin²θ)/(cos θ (1 + cos θ))
= (1 − cos²θ)/(cos θ (1 + cos θ)) [using sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ]
= ((1 − cos θ)(1 + cos θ))/(cos θ (1 + cos θ)) [difference of two squares]
= (1 − cos θ)/(cos θ) [cancelling (1 + cos θ)]
= (1)/(cos θ) − 1
= sec θ − 1
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q6. Prove that: cos4θ = 1 − 8sin²θ cos²θ

Ans: Method: use cos4θ = 2cos²2θ − 1 and then cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ.
L.H.S = cos4θ = cos(2(2θ))
= 2cos²2θ − 1 [by cos2x = 2cos²x − 1 with x = 2θ]
= 2(1 − 2sin²θ)² − 1 [using cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ]
= 2(1 − 4sin²θ + 4sin⁴θ) − 1 [squaring]
= 2 − 8sin²θ + 8sin⁴θ − 1 [expanding]
= 1 − 8sin²θ + 8sin⁴θ
= 1 − 8sin²θ (1 − sin²θ) [taking out 8sin²θ]
= 1 − 8sin²θ cos²θ [using 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ]
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q7. Prove that: sin6x sinx + cos4x cos3x = cos3x cos2x

Ans: Identities used: 2 sin α sin β = cos(α − β) − cos(α + β) and 2 cos α cos β = cos(α + β) + cos(α − β).
sin6x sinx = (1)/(2)[cos(6x − x) − cos(6x + x)] = (1)/(2)[cos5x − cos7x]
cos4x cos3x = (1)/(2)[cos(4x + 3x) + cos(4x − 3x)] = (1)/(2)[cos7x + cos x]
Adding: L.H.S = (1)/(2)[cos5x − cos7x] + (1)/(2)[cos7x + cos x]
= (1)/(2)[cos5x + cos x] [the cos7x terms cancel]
Also R.H.S = cos3x cos2x = (1)/(2)[cos(3x + 2x) + cos(3x − 2x)] = (1)/(2)[cos5x + cos x], the same expression.
Hence L.H.S = R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q8. Prove that: sin((π)/(4) − θ) sin((π)/(4) + θ) = (1)/(2) cos2θ

Ans: Method: expand both factors with the sin(α ∓ β) identities and simplify.
sin((π)/(4) − θ) = sin((π)/(4)) cos θ − cos((π)/(4)) sin θ = (1)/(√2) (cos θ − sin θ) [since sin((π)/(4)) = cos((π)/(4)) = (1)/(√2)]
sin((π)/(4) + θ) = sin((π)/(4)) cos θ + cos((π)/(4)) sin θ = (1)/(√2) (cos θ + sin θ)
Multiplying: L.H.S = (1)/(√2)(cos θ − sin θ) × (1)/(√2)(cos θ + sin θ)
= (1)/(2)(cos²θ − sin²θ) [difference of two squares]
= (1)/(2) cos2θ [by cos2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ]
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q9(i). Prove that: (sin²(π + θ) tan((3π)/(2) + θ))/(cot²((3π)/(2) − θ) cos²(π − θ) cosec(2π − θ)) = cos θ

Ans: Method: reduce every allied angle first, then simplify.
sin(π + θ) = −sin θ, so sin²(π + θ) = sin²θ
tan((3π)/(2) + θ) = −cot θ [allied-angle reduction]
cot((3π)/(2) − θ) = tan θ, so cot²((3π)/(2) − θ) = tan²θ
cos(π − θ) = −cos θ, so cos²(π − θ) = cos²θ
cosec(2π − θ) = −cosec θ
Numerator = sin²θ × (−cot θ) = sin²θ × (−(cos θ)/(sin θ)) = −sin θ cos θ
Denominator = tan²θ × cos²θ × (−cosec θ) = (sin²θ)/(cos²θ) × cos²θ × (−(1)/(sin θ)) = −sin θ
L.H.S = (−sin θ cos θ)/(−sin θ)
= cos θ [cancelling −sin θ]
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q9(ii). Prove that: (cos(90° + θ) sec(−θ) tan(180° − θ))/(sec(360° − θ) sin(180° + θ) cot(90° − θ)) = −1

Ans: Method: reduce every allied angle first, then simplify.
cos(90° + θ) = −sin θ
sec(−θ) = sec θ [sec is an even function]
tan(180° − θ) = −tan θ
sec(360° − θ) = sec θ
sin(180° + θ) = −sin θ
cot(90° − θ) = tan θ
Numerator = (−sin θ) × sec θ × (−tan θ) = sin θ × (1)/(cos θ) × (sin θ)/(cos θ) = (sin²θ)/(cos²θ) = tan²θ
Denominator = sec θ × (−sin θ) × tan θ = (1)/(cos θ) × (−sin θ) × (sin θ)/(cos θ) = −(sin²θ)/(cos²θ) = −tan²θ
L.H.S = (tan²θ)/(−tan²θ)
= −1
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

mcqs.why: The expression matches cos(α + β) = cos α cos β − sin α sin β with α = 50°50′ and β = 9°10′. The angles add to 60°, so the value is cos60° = (1)/(2).

mcqs.q: If tan15° = 2 − √3, then cot²75° = ?
If tan(α + β) = (1)/(2) and tan α = (1)/(3), then tan β = ?
sin θ cos(90° − θ) + cos θ sin(90° − θ) = ?
mcqs.why: cos(90° − θ) = sin θ and sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, so the expression is sin θ sin θ + cos θ cos θ = sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Equivalently it is sin(θ + 90° − θ) = sin90° = 1.

mcqs.q: (sec θ + tan θ)(1 − sin θ) = ?
mcqs.why: sec θ + tan θ = (1)/(cos θ) + (sin θ)/(cos θ) = (1 + sin θ)/(cos θ). Multiply by (1 − sin θ): ((1 + sin θ)(1 − sin θ))/(cos θ) = (1 − sin²θ)/(cos θ) = (cos²θ)/(cos θ) = cos θ.
Use sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B with A = x, B = (π)/(2): sin(x − (π)/(2)) = sin x cos((π)/(2)) − cos x sin((π)/(2)) = sin x (0) − cos x (1) = −cos x.

mcqs.q: A point on the unit circle is in the third quadrant. If the x-coordinate of the point is −(4)/(5), then its y-coordinate is:
mcqs.why: On the unit circle x² + y² = 1: y² = 1 − (16)/(25) = (9)/(25), so y = ±(3)/(5). In the third quadrant y is negative, so y = −(3)/(5).

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an identity?
mcqs.why: sin(2a) = 2 sin a cos a, so sin a cos a = (1)/(2) sin(2a) holds for all a — an identity. The others fail: sin a + cos a = 1 fails at a = 90°, sin(−a) = −sin a not sin a, and tan a = (sin a)/(cos a) not its reciprocal.

mcqs.q: (2sinθ sin2θ)/(cos θ + cos3θ) simplifies to:
mcqs.why: Denominator: cos θ + cos3θ = 2 cos((θ + 3θ)/(2)) cos((3θ − θ)/(2)) = 2 cos2θ cos θ. So the fraction is (2 sin θ sin2θ)/(2 cos2θ cos θ) = ((sin2θ)/(cos2θ)) × ((sin θ)/(cos θ)) = tan2θ tanθ.

mcqs.q: cos4θ expressed in terms of sin θ and cos θ is:
mcqs.why: cos4θ = 2cos²2θ − 1 with cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ: cos4θ = 2(1 − 2sin²θ)² − 1 = 2(1 − 4sin²θ + 4sin⁴θ) − 1 = 1 − 8sin²θ + 8sin⁴θ = 1 − 8sin²θ(1 − sin²θ) = 1 − 8sin²θ cos²θ.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.1
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In a right triangle with γ = 90°, the acute angles are complementary: β = 90° − α; with c = 6 and α = 30°, β = 60°, a = 3 and b = 3√3 ≈ 5.20.
  • With b = 126 and β = 67.3°, c = (b)/(sin β) ≈ 136.6 and a = (b)/(tan β) ≈ 52.7, with α = 22.7°.
  • With c = 10 and β = 45°, both legs are equal: a = b = 5√2 ≈ 7.07 and α = 45°.
  • Height from angle of elevation uses tan: a post 38 m away at 33.23° has height 38 × tan33.23° ≈ 24.89 m.
  • Angle of elevation of the sun from an 82 m minar with 62 m shadow is tan⁻¹((82)/(62)) ≈ 52.9°.
  • For two ships from a 52 m cliff at depressions 36° and 24°, the distances from the foot are ≈ 71.57 m and ≈ 116.79 m, so the ships are ≈ 45.22 m apart.
  • A kite at 35° with 340 m string and 10 m sag has effective length 330 m and height 330 × sin35° ≈ 189.28 m.
  • An isosceles triangle with vertical angle 108° and base 20 cm has base angles 36° and altitude 10 × tan36° ≈ 7.27 cm.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve the right triangle shown in the figure: γ = 90° at C, ∠A = 30°, hypotenuse c = 6; find a, b and β. (Figure: A at the left, C at the bottom right with the right angle, B at the top right; AB = 6, BC = a, AC = b.)

Ans: Method: in a right triangle the acute angles are complementary, and sin/cos of an acute angle give the unknown sides from the hypotenuse.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC is right-angled at C. Vertex A is at the left, C at the bottom right carrying the right angle γ = 90°, and B at the top right. The hypotenuse AB opposite C is c = 6. Side a = BC is the vertical side opposite A, side b = AC is the horizontal side opposite B, and the angle at A is α = 30°. We have to find a, b and the angle β at B.
Step 1: β = 90° − α = 90° − 30° = 60° [acute angles of a right triangle are complementary]
Step 2: sin α = (opposite)/(hypotenuse) = (a)/(c), so a = c sin α = 6 × sin30° = 6 × (1)/(2) = 3
Step 3: cos α = (adjacent)/(hypotenuse) = (b)/(c), so b = c cos α = 6 × cos30° = 6 × (√3)/(2) = 3√3 ≈ 5.20
Answer: a = 3, b = 3√3 ≈ 5.20, β = 60°

Q: Q1(ii). Solve the right triangle shown in the figure: γ = 90° at C, b = 126, β = 67.3°; find a, c and α. (Figure: A at the left, C at the top right with the right angle, B at the bottom right; AC = 126, CB = a, AB = c.)

Ans: Method: in a right triangle the acute angles are complementary, and the sine rule for a right triangle, sin β = (opposite side b)/(hypotenuse c), gives the hypotenuse.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC is right-angled at C. Vertex A is at the left, C at the top right carrying the right angle γ = 90°, and B at the bottom right. Side b = AC = 126 is the upper side, opposite the angle β = 67.3° at B. Side a = CB is opposite A, and the hypotenuse AB opposite C is c. We have to find a, c and the angle α at A.
Step 1: α = 90° − β = 90° − 67.3° = 22.7° [acute angles of a right triangle are complementary]
Step 2: sin β = (b)/(c), so c = (b)/(sin β) = (126)/(sin67.3°) = (126)/(0.9222) ≈ 136.6
Step 3: tan β = (b)/(a), so a = (b)/(tan β) = (126)/(tan67.3°) = (126)/(2.390) ≈ 52.7
Answer: a ≈ 52.7, c ≈ 136.6, α = 22.7°

Q: Q1(iii). Solve the right triangle shown in the figure: γ = 90° at C, hypotenuse c = 10, β = 45°; find a, b and α. (Figure: A at the top, C at the bottom left with the right angle, B at the bottom right; AB = 10, CB = a, AC = b.)

Ans: Method: in a right triangle the acute angles are complementary, and sin/cos of 45° give the two equal legs from the hypotenuse.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC is right-angled at C. Vertex A is at the top, C at the bottom left carrying the right angle γ = 90°, and B at the bottom right. The hypotenuse AB opposite C is c = 10. Side a = CB is the horizontal base opposite A, side b = AC is the vertical side opposite the angle β = 45° at B. We have to find a, b and the angle α at A.
Step 1: α = 90° − β = 90° − 45° = 45° [acute angles of a right triangle are complementary]
Step 2: sin β = (b)/(c), so b = c sin β = 10 × sin45° = 10 × (√2)/(2) = 5√2 ≈ 7.07
Step 3: cos β = (a)/(c), so a = c cos β = 10 × cos45° = 10 × (√2)/(2) = 5√2 ≈ 7.07
Answer: a = 5√2 ≈ 7.07, b = 5√2 ≈ 7.07, α = 45°

Q: Q2(i). Solve the right triangle ABC in which γ = 90° and: a = 14, β = 28°

Ans: Method: γ = 90°, so use complementary angles and the right-triangle ratios sin α = (a)/(c) and tan β = (b)/(a).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC is right-angled at C (γ = 90°). Side a = BC = 14 is opposite the angle α at A, side b = AC is opposite the given angle β = 28° at B, and the hypotenuse AB opposite C is c. We have to find α, b and c.
Step 1: α = 90° − β = 90° − 28° = 62°
Step 2: sin α = (a)/(c), so c = (a)/(sin α) = (14)/(sin62°) = (14)/(0.8829) ≈ 15.86
Step 3: tan β = (b)/(a), so b = a tan β = 14 × tan28° = 14 × 0.5317 ≈ 7.44
Answer: α = 62°, b ≈ 7.44, c ≈ 15.86

Q: Q2(ii). Solve the right triangle ABC in which γ = 90° and: b = 8.9, β = 21.5°

Ans: Method: γ = 90°, so use complementary angles and the right-triangle ratios sin β = (b)/(c) and tan α = (a)/(b).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC is right-angled at C (γ = 90°). Side b = AC = 8.9 is opposite the given angle β = 21.5° at B, side a = BC is opposite the angle α at A, and the hypotenuse AB opposite C is c. We have to find α, a and c.
Step 1: α = 90° − β = 90° − 21.5° = 68.5°
Step 2: sin β = (b)/(c), so c = (b)/(sin β) = (8.9)/(sin21.5°) = (8.9)/(0.3665) ≈ 24.28
Step 3: tan α = (a)/(b), so a = b tan α = 8.9 × tan68.5° = 8.9 × 2.5386 ≈ 22.59
Answer: α = 68.5°, a ≈ 22.59, c ≈ 24.28

Q: Q2(iii). Solve the right triangle ABC in which γ = 90° and: b = 14, c = 450

Ans: Method: γ = 90°, so the hypotenuse is c = 450; use Pythagoras for a and sin β = (b)/(c) for the angles.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC is right-angled at C (γ = 90°). The hypotenuse AB opposite C is c = 450, side b = AC = 14 is opposite the angle β at B, and side a = BC is opposite the angle α at A. We have to find a, α and β.
Step 1: by Pythagoras, a² = c² − b² = 450² − 14² = 202500 − 196 = 202304
So a = √202304 ≈ 449.78
Step 2: sin β = (b)/(c) = (14)/(450) = 0.03111, so β = sin⁻¹(0.03111) ≈ 1.78°
Step 3: α = 90° − β ≈ 90° − 1.78° = 88.22°
Answer: a ≈ 449.78, α ≈ 88.22°, β ≈ 1.78°

Q: Q3. The angle of elevation of the top of a post from a point on level ground 38 m away is 33.23°. Find the height of the post.

Ans: Method: the post, the ground and the line of sight form a right triangle; use tan(angle of elevation) = (height)/(ground distance).
Diagram (in words): Let F be the foot of the vertical post and T its top. P is the observation point on level ground, 38 m from F, so PF = 38 m is the horizontal side. The angle of elevation of T from P is ∠FPT = 33.23°. Triangle PFT is right-angled at F, and the height of the post is TF, which we have to find.
Step 1: in ΔPFT, tan33.23° = (TF)/(PF) = (TF)/(38)
Step 2: TF = 38 × tan33.23°
Step 3: TF = 38 × 0.6551 ≈ 24.89
Answer: The height of the post is ≈ 24.89 m

Q: Q4. A masjid minar 82 meters high casts a shadow 62 meters long. Find the angle of elevation of the sun at that moment.

Ans: Method: the minar and its shadow form a right triangle; use tan(angle of elevation of the sun) = (height)/(shadow length).
Diagram (in words): Let F be the foot of the vertical minar and T its top, so TF = 82 m. The shadow runs along the level ground from F to a point S, with FS = 62 m. The sun's rays pass through T and S, so the angle of elevation of the sun is the angle θ at S in the right triangle TFS, right-angled at F. We have to find θ.
Step 1: in ΔTFS, tan θ = (TF)/(FS) = (82)/(62)
Step 2: tan θ = 1.3226
Step 3: θ = tan⁻¹(1.3226) ≈ 52.9°
Answer: The angle of elevation of the sun is ≈ 52.9°

Q: Q5. The angle of depression of a boat 65.7 m from the base of a cliff is 28.9°. How high is the cliff?

Ans: Method: the angle of depression from the top of the cliff equals the angle of elevation from the boat (alternate angles); use tan = (height)/(horizontal distance).
Diagram (in words): Let F be the base of the vertical cliff and T its top; the height TF is to be found. The boat is at B on the water with FB = 65.7 m horizontal. The angle of depression of B from T is 28.9°, so the angle of elevation of T from B is also 28.9°. Triangle TFB is right-angled at F.
Step 1: in ΔTFB, tan28.9° = (TF)/(FB) = (TF)/(65.7)
Step 2: TF = 65.7 × tan28.9°
Step 3: TF = 65.7 × 0.5520 ≈ 36.27
Answer: The cliff is ≈ 36.3 m high

Q: Q6. From the top of a cliff 52 m high the angles of depression of two ships due east of it are 36° and 24° respectively. Find the distance between the ships.

Ans: Method: find the distance of each ship from the foot of the cliff using tan of its angle of depression, then subtract.
Diagram (in words): Let T be the top of the cliff and F its foot, with TF = 52 m vertical. The two ships S₁ (nearer) and S₂ (farther) lie due east of the cliff on the same horizontal line through F. The angle of depression of S₁ from T is 36° and of S₂ is 24°; these equal the angles of elevation at the ships. We have to find S₁S₂ = FS₂ − FS₁.
Step 1: for the nearer ship, tan36° = (52)/(FS₁), so FS₁ = (52)/(tan36°) = (52)/(0.7265) ≈ 71.57 m
Step 2: for the farther ship, tan24° = (52)/(FS₂), so FS₂ = (52)/(tan24°) = (52)/(0.4452) ≈ 116.79 m
Step 3: distance between the ships = FS₂ − FS₁ ≈ 116.79 − 71.57 = 45.22 m
Answer: The ships are ≈ 45.2 m apart (the book's key gives 45.3 m)

Q: Q7. Two masts are 20 m and 12 m high. If the line joining their tops makes an angle of 35° with the horizontal; find their distance apart.

Ans: Method: the difference of the heights and the distance apart form a right triangle with the joining line; use tan35° = (difference of heights)/(distance apart).
Diagram (in words): Two vertical masts stand on level ground, one 20 m high with top A and one 12 m high with top B. Draw a horizontal line from B meeting the taller mast at point D; then DB is the distance between the masts, AD = 20 − 12 = 8 m is the vertical difference, and the line AB joining the tops makes an angle of 35° with the horizontal DB. Triangle ADB is right-angled at D. We have to find DB.
Step 1: in ΔADB, tan35° = (AD)/(DB) = (8)/(DB)
Step 2: DB = (8)/(tan35°) = (8)/(0.7002) ≈ 11.43
Answer: The masts are ≈ 11.43 m apart

Q: Q8. The measure of the angle of elevation of a kite is 35°. The string of the kite is 340 meters long. If the sag in the string is 10 meters, find the height of the kite.

Ans: Method: the sag shortens the effective straight length of the string to 340 − 10 = 330 m; use sin(angle of elevation) = (height)/(string length).
Diagram (in words): Let G be the point on the ground where the string is held and K the kite. Because of the 10 m sag, the straight-line distance GK is 340 − 10 = 330 m, acting as the hypotenuse of a right triangle whose vertical side is the height h of the kite above the ground. The angle of elevation of K from G is 35°. We have to find h.
Step 1: effective string length = 340 − 10 = 330 m
Step 2: sin35° = (h)/(330), so h = 330 × sin35°
Step 3: h = 330 × 0.5736 ≈ 189.28
Answer: The height of the kite is ≈ 189.3 m

Q: Q9. A parachutist is descending vertically. How far does the parachutist fall as the angle of elevation changes from 50° to 30°, observed from a point 100 m away from the feet of the parachutist where he touches the ground?

Ans: Method: find the parachutist's height at each angle of elevation using tan, then subtract the two heights.
Diagram (in words): Let L be the point where the parachutist touches the ground and O the observation point, with OL = 100 m horizontal. The parachutist descends vertically along the line through L. At the higher position P₁ the angle of elevation from O is 50°, and at the lower position P₂ it is 30°. Triangles OLP₁ and OLP₂ are right-angled at L. We have to find the fall P₁P₂ = LP₁ − LP₂. (Note: the question measures the distances in metres; the book's answer key prints the unit as feet, but the value is in metres.)
Step 1: in ΔOLP₁, tan50° = (LP₁)/(100), so LP₁ = 100 × tan50° = 100 × 1.1918 ≈ 119.18 m
Step 2: in ΔOLP₂, tan30° = (LP₂)/(100), so LP₂ = 100 × tan30° = 100 × 0.5774 ≈ 57.74 m
Step 3: fall = LP₁ − LP₂ ≈ 119.18 − 57.74 = 61.44 m
Answer: The parachutist falls ≈ 61.44 m

Q: Q10. An isosceles triangle has a vertical angle of 108° and a base 20 cm long. Calculate its altitude.

Ans: Method: the altitude from the vertex bisects both the vertical angle and the base; use tan of a base angle in the resulting right triangle.
Diagram (in words): The isosceles triangle has vertex V at the top with vertical angle 108°, and a horizontal base of 20 cm. The altitude from V meets the base at its midpoint M, splitting the base into two parts of 10 cm each. Each base angle is (180° − 108°)/(2) = 36°. In the right triangle formed, the altitude h is opposite the 36° base angle and the adjacent side is 10 cm. We have to find h.
Step 1: base angle = (180° − 108°)/(2) = (72°)/(2) = 36°
Step 2: half of the base = (20)/(2) = 10 cm
Step 3: tan36° = (h)/(10), so h = 10 × tan36°
Step 4: h = 10 × 0.7265 ≈ 7.27 cm
Answer: The altitude is ≈ 7.27 cm (7.265 cm)

mcqs.q: In ΔABC with γ = 90°, α = 30° and hypotenuse c = 6, what is side a opposite α?
mcqs.why: Use a = c sin α. Substitute: a = 6 × sin30° = 6 × (1)/(2) = 3. So side a = 3.

mcqs.q: In ΔABC with γ = 90°, α = 30° and hypotenuse c = 6, what is side b?
mcqs.why: Use b = c cos α. Substitute: b = 6 × cos30° = 6 × (√3)/(2) = 3√3 ≈ 5.20. So side b = 3√3 ≈ 5.20.

mcqs.q: In a right triangle with γ = 90°, b = 126 and β = 67.3°, what is the hypotenuse c?
In a right triangle with γ = 90°, c = 10 and β = 45°, what is α?
mcqs.why: Acute angles are complementary: α = 90° − β. Substitute: α = 90° − 45° = 45°. So α = 45°.

mcqs.q: Solve the right triangle with γ = 90°, a = 14 and β = 28°. What is c?
In a right triangle with γ = 90°, b = 14 and c = 450, what is a?
The angle of elevation of the top of a post from a point 38 m away is 33.23°. What is the height of the post?
mcqs.why: Use tan(elevation) = (height)/(distance). So height = 38 × tan33.23° = 38 × 0.6551 ≈ 24.89 m. The post is ≈ 24.89 m high.

mcqs.q: A minar 82 m high casts a shadow 62 m long. What is the angle of elevation of the sun?
mcqs.why: Use tan θ = (height)/(shadow) = (82)/(62) = 1.3226. Then θ = tan⁻¹(1.3226) ≈ 52.9°. So the elevation is ≈ 52.9°.

mcqs.q: From a 52 m cliff the angles of depression of two ships are 36° and 24°. What is the distance between the ships?
Two masts are 20 m and 12 m high and the line joining their tops makes 35° with the horizontal. How far apart are they?
mcqs.why: Height difference = 20 − 12 = 8 m. Use tan35° = (8)/(distance), so distance = (8)/(tan35°) = (8)/(0.7002) ≈ 11.43 m. The masts are ≈ 11.43 m apart.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.2
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • SSS with a = 209, b = 120, c = 241 gives γ = 90° because 209² + 120² = 241², with α ≈ 60°08′ and β ≈ 29°52′.
  • SAS with a = 120, b = 240, γ = 32° gives c = √23152 ≈ 152.16 by the cosine law, α ≈ 24°42′ and β ≈ 123°18′.
  • With α = 100°, c = 345, γ = 56.4°, the sine law gives a ≈ 407.91 and b ≈ 165.83, with β = 23.6°.
  • No triangle exists for a = 37.5, b = 12.4, β = 72°, because sin α = (37.5 × sin72°)/(12.4) ≈ 2.88 > 1.
  • Half-sine law: for a = 74, b = 52, c = 47, S = 86.5 and the largest angle α ≈ 96°37′ opposite the largest side.
  • A parallelogram diagonal of 20 cm making angles 20° and 40° with the sides gives sides ≈ 7.90 cm and ≈ 14.84 cm by the sine law.
  • Two planes at 525 km/h for 2 h fly 1050 km each at 127° to each other and end ≈ 1879.4 km apart by the cosine law.
  • Cosine-law identities: 1 + cos α = ((b + c + a)(b + c − a))/(2bc) and 1 − cos α = ((a − b + c)(a + b − c))/(2bc).

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: a = 209, b = 120, c = 241

Ans: Method: all three sides are given (SSS), so use the cosine law cos α = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc) for each angle.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has vertices A, B, C with the standard notation: side a = BC = 209 opposite α, side b = CA = 120 opposite β, and side c = AB = 241 opposite γ. All three sides are known; we have to find α, β and γ.
Step 1: cos α = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc) = (120² + 241² − 209²)/(2 × 120 × 241) = (14400 + 58081 − 43681)/(57840) = (28800)/(57840) = 0.4979
So α = cos⁻¹(0.4979) ≈ 60°08′
Step 2: cos β = (a² + c² − b²)/(2ac) = (209² + 241² − 120²)/(2 × 209 × 241) = (43681 + 58081 − 14400)/(100738) = (87362)/(100738) = 0.8672
So β = cos⁻¹(0.8672) ≈ 29°52′
Step 3: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 60°08′ − 29°52′ = 90°00′
Check: 209² + 120² = 43681 + 14400 = 58081 = 241², confirming γ = 90°.
Answer: α ≈ 60°08′, β ≈ 29°52′, γ = 90° (the book's key rounds these to α = 60°, β = 30°, γ = 90°)

Q: Q1(ii). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: a = 120, b = 240, γ = 32°

Ans: Method: two sides and the included angle are given (SAS), so find c by the cosine law, then an angle by the sine law.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: side a = BC = 120 opposite α, side b = CA = 240 opposite β, and the included angle between them at C is γ = 32°. Side c = AB opposite γ is unknown. We have to find c, α and β.
Step 1 (cosine law): c² = a² + b² − 2ab cos γ = 120² + 240² − 2(120)(240) cos32°
= 14400 + 57600 − 57600 × 0.84805 = 72000 − 48848 = 23152
So c = √23152 ≈ 152.16
Step 2 (sine law): (sin α)/(a) = (sin γ)/(c), so sin α = (a sin γ)/(c) = (120 × sin32°)/(152.16) = (120 × 0.52992)/(152.16) = 0.41790
So α = sin⁻¹(0.41790) ≈ 24°42′
Step 3: β = 180° − γ − α ≈ 180° − 32° − 24°42′ = 123°18′
Answer: c ≈ 152.16, α ≈ 24°42′, β ≈ 123°18′

Q: Q1(iii). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: α = 100°, c = 345, γ = 56.4°

Ans: Method: two angles and a side are given, so find the third angle and use the sine law for the remaining sides.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: the angle at A is α = 100°, the angle at C is γ = 56.4°, and side c = AB = 345 opposite γ. We have to find β and sides a = BC and b = CA.
Step 1: β = 180° − α − γ = 180° − 100° − 56.4° = 23.6°
Step 2 (sine law): (a)/(sin α) = (c)/(sin γ), so a = (c sin α)/(sin γ) = (345 × sin100°)/(sin56.4°) = (345 × 0.98481)/(0.83389) ≈ 407.91
Step 3 (sine law): b = (c sin β)/(sin γ) = (345 × sin23.6°)/(sin56.4°) = (345 × 0.40035)/(0.83389) ≈ 165.83
Answer: β = 23.6°, a ≈ 407.91, b ≈ 165.83

Q: Q1(iv). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: a = 24.5, c = 43.8, β = 112°

Ans: Method: two sides and the included angle are given (SAS), so find b by the cosine law, then an angle by the sine law.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: side a = BC = 24.5 opposite α, side c = AB = 43.8 opposite γ, and the included angle between them at B is β = 112°. Side b = CA opposite β is unknown. We have to find b, α and γ.
Step 1 (cosine law): b² = a² + c² − 2ac cos β = 24.5² + 43.8² − 2(24.5)(43.8) cos112°
= 600.25 + 1918.44 − 2146.2 × (−0.37461) = 2518.69 + 804.04 = 3322.73
So b = √3322.73 ≈ 57.64
Step 2 (sine law): sin α = (a sin β)/(b) = (24.5 × sin112°)/(57.64) = (24.5 × 0.92718)/(57.64) = 0.39412
So α = sin⁻¹(0.39412) ≈ 23°13′
Step 3: γ = 180° − β − α ≈ 180° − 112° − 23°13′ = 44°47′
Answer: b ≈ 57.64, α ≈ 23°13′, γ ≈ 44°47′

Q: Q1(v). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: b = 1.6, c = 3.2, α = 100°24′

Ans: Method: two sides and the included angle are given (SAS), so find a by the cosine law, then an angle by the sine law.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: side b = CA = 1.6 opposite β, side c = AB = 3.2 opposite γ, and the included angle between them at A is α = 100°24′. Side a = BC opposite α is unknown. We have to find a, β and γ.
Step 1 (cosine law): a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos α = 1.6² + 3.2² − 2(1.6)(3.2) cos100°24′
= 2.56 + 10.24 − 10.24 × (−0.18052) = 12.80 + 1.85 = 14.65
So a = √14.65 ≈ 3.83
Step 2 (sine law): sin β = (b sin α)/(a) = (1.6 × sin100°24′)/(3.83) = (1.6 × 0.98357)/(3.83) = 0.41119
So β = sin⁻¹(0.41119) ≈ 24°17′
Step 3: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 100°24′ − 24°17′ = 55°19′
Answer: a ≈ 3.83, β ≈ 24°17′, γ ≈ 55°19′

Q: Q1(vi). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: β = 39°30′, γ = 34°10′, a = 240

Ans: Method: two angles and a side are given, so find the third angle and use the sine law for the remaining sides.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: the angle at B is β = 39°30′, the angle at C is γ = 34°10′, and side a = BC = 240 opposite the unknown angle α at A. We have to find α and sides b = CA and c = AB.
Step 1: α = 180° − β − γ = 180° − 39°30′ − 34°10′ = 106°20′
Step 2 (sine law): b = (a sin β)/(sin α) = (240 × sin39°30′)/(sin106°20′) = (240 × 0.63608)/(0.95947) ≈ 159.08
Step 3 (sine law): c = (a sin γ)/(sin α) = (240 × sin34°10′)/(sin106°20′) = (240 × 0.56160)/(0.95947) ≈ 140.45
Answer: α = 106°20′, b ≈ 159.08, c ≈ 140.45

Q: Q1(vii). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: α = 35°, β = 70°, c = 115

Ans: Method: two angles and a side are given, so find the third angle and use the sine law for the remaining sides.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: the angle at A is α = 35°, the angle at B is β = 70°, and side c = AB = 115 opposite the unknown angle γ at C. We have to find γ and sides a = BC and b = CA.
Step 1: γ = 180° − α − β = 180° − 35° − 70° = 75°
Step 2 (sine law): a = (c sin α)/(sin γ) = (115 × sin35°)/(sin75°) = (115 × 0.57358)/(0.96593) ≈ 68.29
Step 3 (sine law): b = (c sin β)/(sin γ) = (115 × sin70°)/(sin75°) = (115 × 0.93969)/(0.96593) ≈ 111.88
Answer: γ = 75°, a ≈ 68.29, b ≈ 111.88

Q: Q1(viii). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: a = 37.5, b = 12.4, β = 72°

Ans: Method: try the sine law to find α from the given side-angle pair.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: side a = BC = 37.5 opposite the unknown angle α at A, side b = CA = 12.4 opposite the given angle β = 72° at B, and side c = AB opposite γ. We would have to find α, γ and c.
Step 1 (sine law): (sin α)/(a) = (sin β)/(b), so sin α = (a sin β)/(b)
Step 2: sin α = (37.5 × sin72°)/(12.4) = (37.5 × 0.95106)/(12.4) = (35.66)/(12.4) ≈ 2.88
Step 3: but sin α can never be greater than 1, so no angle α exists for these dimensions.
Answer: No triangle is possible with the given dimensions (the book's answer key also gives: No triangle possible)

Q: Q1(ix). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: b = 12.5, c = 23, α = 38°20′

Ans: Method: two sides and the included angle are given (SAS), so find a by the cosine law, then an angle by the sine law.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: side b = CA = 12.5 opposite β, side c = AB = 23 opposite γ, and the included angle between them at A is α = 38°20′. Side a = BC opposite α is unknown. We have to find a, β and γ.
Step 1 (cosine law): a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos α = 12.5² + 23² − 2(12.5)(23) cos38°20′
= 156.25 + 529 − 575 × 0.78410 = 685.25 − 450.86 = 234.39
So a = √234.39 ≈ 15.31
Step 2 (sine law): sin β = (b sin α)/(a) = (12.5 × sin38°20′)/(15.31) = (12.5 × 0.61909)/(15.31) = 0.50548
So β = sin⁻¹(0.50548) ≈ 30°26′
Step 3: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 38°20′ − 30°26′ = 111°14′
Answer: a ≈ 15.31, β ≈ 30°26′, γ ≈ 111°14′

Q: Q1(x). Solve the triangle with the given dimensions: a = 168, c = 319, β = 110°22′

Ans: Method: two sides and the included angle are given (SAS), so find b by the cosine law, then an angle by the sine law.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation: side a = BC = 168 opposite α, side c = AB = 319 opposite γ, and the included angle between them at B is β = 110°22′. Side b = CA opposite β is unknown. We have to find b, α and γ.
Step 1 (cosine law): b² = a² + c² − 2ac cos β = 168² + 319² − 2(168)(319) cos110°22′
= 28224 + 101761 − 107184 × (−0.34899) = 129985 + 37407 = 167392
So b = √167392 ≈ 409.01
Step 2 (sine law): sin α = (a sin β)/(b) = (168 × sin110°22′)/(409.01) = (168 × 0.93716)/(409.01) = 0.38493
So α = sin⁻¹(0.38493) ≈ 22°39′
Step 3: γ = 180° − β − α ≈ 180° − 110°22′ − 22°39′ = 46°59′
Answer: b ≈ 409.01, α ≈ 22°39′, γ ≈ 46°59′

Q: Q2(i). Find the angle of largest measure (using half sine law): a = 74, b = 52 and c = 47

Ans: Method: the largest angle is opposite the largest side. Here a = 74 is the largest side, so find α using the half-angle sine formula sin(α/2) = √((S − b)(S − c)/(bc)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation with sides a = BC = 74, b = CA = 52 and c = AB = 47. Since a is the longest side, the angle α at A, opposite a, is the largest angle. We have to find α.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(74 + 52 + 47) = (173)/(2) = 86.5
Step 2: S − b = 86.5 − 52 = 34.5 and S − c = 86.5 − 47 = 39.5
Step 3: sin(α/2) = √((34.5 × 39.5)/(52 × 47)) = √((1362.75)/(2444)) = √0.55759 ≈ 0.74672
Step 4: (α)/(2) = sin⁻¹(0.74672) ≈ 48°19′, so α ≈ 96°37′
Answer: The largest angle is α ≈ 96°37′

Q: Q2(ii). Find the angle of largest measure (using half sine law): a = 7, b = 9 and c = 7

Ans: Method: the largest angle is opposite the largest side. Here b = 9 is the largest side, so find β using the half-angle sine formula sin(β/2) = √((S − a)(S − c)/(ac)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation with sides a = BC = 7, b = CA = 9 and c = AB = 7. Since b is the longest side, the angle β at B, opposite b, is the largest angle. We have to find β.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(7 + 9 + 7) = (23)/(2) = 11.5
Step 2: S − a = 11.5 − 7 = 4.5 and S − c = 11.5 − 7 = 4.5
Step 3: sin(β/2) = √((4.5 × 4.5)/(7 × 7)) = (4.5)/(7) ≈ 0.64286
Step 4: (β)/(2) = sin⁻¹(0.64286) ≈ 40°00′, so β ≈ 80°01′
Answer: The largest angle is β ≈ 80°01′ (about 80°)

Q: Q2(iii). Find the angle of largest measure (using half sine law): a = 2.3, b = 1.5 and c = 2.7

Ans: Method: the largest angle is opposite the largest side. Here c = 2.7 is the largest side, so find γ using the half-angle sine formula sin(γ/2) = √((S − a)(S − b)/(ab)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation with sides a = BC = 2.3, b = CA = 1.5 and c = AB = 2.7. Since c is the longest side, the angle γ at C, opposite c, is the largest angle. We have to find γ.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(2.3 + 1.5 + 2.7) = (6.5)/(2) = 3.25
Step 2: S − a = 3.25 − 2.3 = 0.95 and S − b = 3.25 − 1.5 = 1.75
Step 3: sin(γ/2) = √((0.95 × 1.75)/(2.3 × 1.5)) = √((1.6625)/(3.45)) = √0.48188 ≈ 0.69418
Step 4: (γ)/(2) = sin⁻¹(0.69418) ≈ 43°58′, so γ ≈ 87°55′
Answer: The largest angle is γ ≈ 87°55′

Q: Q3(i). Solve the triangle for which the lengths of three sides are given (using half cosine law): a = 9, b = 7 and c = 5

Ans: Method: use the half-angle cosine formulas cos(α/2) = √(S(S − a)/(bc)) and cos(β/2) = √(S(S − b)/(ac)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c); then γ = 180° − α − β.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation with sides a = BC = 9, b = CA = 7 and c = AB = 5, opposite the angles α, β and γ respectively. All three sides are known; we have to find all three angles.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(9 + 7 + 5) = (21)/(2) = 10.5; S − a = 1.5, S − b = 3.5, S − c = 5.5
Step 2: cos(α/2) = √(S(S − a)/(bc)) = √((10.5 × 1.5)/(7 × 5)) = √(0.45) ≈ 0.67082
So (α)/(2) ≈ 47°52′ and α ≈ 95°44′
Step 3: cos(β/2) = √(S(S − b)/(ac)) = √((10.5 × 3.5)/(9 × 5)) = √(0.81667) ≈ 0.90370
So (β)/(2) ≈ 25°21′ and β ≈ 50°42′
Step 4: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 95°44′ − 50°42′ = 33°33′
Answer: α ≈ 95°44′, β ≈ 50°42′, γ ≈ 33°33′

Q: Q3(ii). Solve the triangle for which the lengths of three sides are given (using half cosine law): a = 1.2, b = 9 and c = 10

Ans: Method: use the half-angle cosine formulas cos(α/2) = √(S(S − a)/(bc)) and cos(β/2) = √(S(S − b)/(ac)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c); then γ = 180° − α − β.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation with sides a = BC = 1.2, b = CA = 9 and c = AB = 10, opposite the angles α, β and γ respectively. All three sides are known; we have to find all three angles.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(1.2 + 9 + 10) = (20.2)/(2) = 10.1; S − a = 8.9, S − b = 1.1, S − c = 0.1
Step 2: cos(α/2) = √(S(S − a)/(bc)) = √((10.1 × 8.9)/(9 × 10)) = √(0.99889) ≈ 0.99939
So (α)/(2) ≈ 2°00′ and α ≈ 4°00′
Step 3: cos(β/2) = √(S(S − b)/(ac)) = √((10.1 × 1.1)/(1.2 × 10)) = √(0.92583) ≈ 0.96220
So (β)/(2) ≈ 15°48′ and β ≈ 31°36′
Step 4: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 4°00′ − 31°36′ = 144°24′
Answer: α ≈ 4°00′, β ≈ 31°36′, γ ≈ 144°24′

Q: Q3(iii). Solve the triangle for which the lengths of three sides are given (using half cosine law): a = 6, b = 8 and c = 12

Ans: Method: use the half-angle cosine formulas cos(α/2) = √(S(S − a)/(bc)) and cos(β/2) = √(S(S − b)/(ac)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c); then γ = 180° − α − β.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has the standard notation with sides a = BC = 6, b = CA = 8 and c = AB = 12, opposite the angles α, β and γ respectively. All three sides are known; we have to find all three angles.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(6 + 8 + 12) = (26)/(2) = 13; S − a = 7, S − b = 5, S − c = 1
Step 2: cos(α/2) = √(S(S − a)/(bc)) = √((13 × 7)/(8 × 12)) = √(0.94792) ≈ 0.97373
So (α)/(2) ≈ 13°11′ and α ≈ 26°23′
Step 3: cos(β/2) = √(S(S − b)/(ac)) = √((13 × 5)/(6 × 12)) = √(0.90278) ≈ 0.95015
So (β)/(2) ≈ 18°10′ and β ≈ 36°20′
Step 4: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 26°23′ − 36°20′ = 117°17′
Answer: α ≈ 26°23′, β ≈ 36°20′, γ ≈ 117°17′

Q: Q4. One diagonal of a parallelogram is 20 cm long and at one end forms angles 20° and 40° with the sides of the parallelogram. Find the length of the sides.

Ans: Method: the diagonal and the two sides form a triangle whose third angle is 180° − 20° − 40° = 120°; apply the sine law in that triangle.
Diagram (in words): Let ABCD be the parallelogram and AC = 20 cm the diagonal drawn from vertex A. At A the diagonal makes an angle of 20° with one side and 40° with the other side. In the triangle ABC formed by the diagonal and the two sides, the angles at A and C are 20° and 40° in some order (alternate interior angles), so the third angle is 120°. The two sides of the parallelogram are the sides of this triangle opposite the 20° and 40° angles. We have to find those two sides.
Step 1: third angle of the triangle = 180° − 20° − 40° = 120°
Step 2 (sine law): side opposite 20° = (20 × sin20°)/(sin120°) = (20 × 0.34202)/(0.86603) ≈ 7.90 cm
Step 3 (sine law): side opposite 40° = (20 × sin40°)/(sin120°) = (20 × 0.64279)/(0.86603) ≈ 14.84 cm
Answer: The sides of the parallelogram are ≈ 7.9 cm and ≈ 14.8 cm

Q: Q5. Two planes start from Karachi International Airport at the same time and fly in directions that make an angle of 127° with each other. Their speeds are 525 km/h. How far apart are they at the end of 2 hours of flying time?

Ans: Method: each plane covers 525 × 2 = 1050 km; the two paths and the distance between the planes form an isosceles triangle, so use the cosine law.
Diagram (in words): Let O be Karachi International Airport. After 2 hours the planes are at P and Q, with OP = OQ = 1050 km along the two flight directions, and the angle between the directions is ∠POQ = 127°. Triangle POQ is isosceles with the side PQ, the distance between the planes, to be found.
Step 1: distance flown by each plane = speed × time = 525 × 2 = 1050 km
Step 2 (cosine law): PQ² = OP² + OQ² − 2(OP)(OQ) cos127°
= 1050² + 1050² − 2(1050)(1050) × (−0.60182)
= 1102500 + 1102500 + 1327015 = 3532015
Step 3: PQ = √3532015 ≈ 1879.4 km
Answer: The planes are ≈ 1879 km apart

Q: Q6. A city block is bounded by three streets. If the measures of the sides of the block are 285, 375 and 396 meters, find the measures of the angles the streets make with each other.

Ans: Method: the block is a triangle with three known sides (SSS); use the cosine law for each angle.
Diagram (in words): The city block is a triangle whose sides, the three streets, measure a = 285 m, b = 375 m and c = 396 m. The angles of the triangle, at the three street corners, are α opposite 285, β opposite 375 and γ opposite 396. We have to find α, β and γ.
Step 1: cos α = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc) = (375² + 396² − 285²)/(2 × 375 × 396) = (140625 + 156816 − 81225)/(297000) = (216216)/(297000) = 0.72803
So α = cos⁻¹(0.72803) ≈ 43°17′
Step 2: cos β = (a² + c² − b²)/(2ac) = (285² + 396² − 375²)/(2 × 285 × 396) = (81225 + 156816 − 140625)/(225720) = (97416)/(225720) = 0.43157
So β = cos⁻¹(0.43157) ≈ 64°26′
Step 3: γ = 180° − α − β ≈ 180° − 43°17′ − 64°26′ = 72°17′
Answer: The streets make angles of ≈ 43°17′, 64°26′ and 72°17′ with each other

Q: Q7. The diagonal of a parallelogram meets the sides at an angle of 30° and 40°. If the length of the diagonal is 30.0 cm, then find the perimeter of the parallelogram.

Ans: Method: the diagonal and the two sides form a triangle whose third angle is 180° − 30° − 40° = 110°; find the sides by the sine law, then double their sum for the perimeter.
Diagram (in words): Let ABCD be the parallelogram with diagonal AC = 30.0 cm. At one end the diagonal makes angles of 30° and 40° with the two sides, so in the triangle formed by the diagonal and the two sides the angles are 30°, 40° and 110°. The sides of the parallelogram are opposite the 30° and 40° angles. We have to find the perimeter 2(sum of the two sides).
Step 1: third angle = 180° − 30° − 40° = 110°
Step 2 (sine law): one side = (30 × sin30°)/(sin110°) = (30 × 0.5)/(0.93969) ≈ 15.96 cm
Step 3 (sine law): other side = (30 × sin40°)/(sin110°) = (30 × 0.64279)/(0.93969) ≈ 20.52 cm
Step 4: perimeter = 2 × (15.96 + 20.52) = 2 × 36.48 ≈ 72.97 cm
Answer: The perimeter is ≈ 72.97 cm (the book's key gives 72.9 cm)

Q: Q8(i). Use the law of cosines to prove: 1 + cos α = ((b + c + a)(b + c − a))/(2bc)

Ans: Law used: the cosine law, cos α = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc).
R.H.S side working is not needed; start from the left side.
1 + cos α = 1 + (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc) [substituting the cosine law]
= (2bc + b² + c² − a²)/(2bc) [taking the common denominator 2bc]
The numerator is (b + c)² − a², since (b + c)² = b² + 2bc + c².
= ((b + c)² − a²)/(2bc)
= ((b + c + a)(b + c − a))/(2bc) [difference of two squares]
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Q: Q8(ii). Use the law of cosines to prove: 1 − cos α = ((a − b + c)(a + b − c))/(2bc)

Ans: Law used: the cosine law, cos α = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc).
1 − cos α = 1 − (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc) [substituting the cosine law]
= (2bc − b² − c² + a²)/(2bc) [taking the common denominator 2bc]
The numerator is a² − (b − c)², since (b − c)² = b² − 2bc + c².
= (a² − (b − c)²)/(2bc)
= ((a − (b − c))(a + (b − c)))/(2bc) [difference of two squares]
= ((a − b + c)(a + b − c))/(2bc)
= R.H.S
Hence proved.

Key Points

  • SAS area Δ = (1)/(2)ab sin γ: with a = 15, b = 80, γ = 38°, Δ = 600 × sin38° ≈ 369.40 square units.
  • SAS area with b = 14, c = 12, α = 82° gives Δ = 84 × sin82° ≈ 83.18 square units.
  • SAA area needs the third angle first: with a = 30, β = 50°, γ = 100°, α = 30° and Δ ≈ 678.97 square units.
  • Heron's formula for SSS: with a = 7.0, b = 8.0, c = 2.0, S = 8.5 and Δ = √41.4375 ≈ 6.44 square units.
  • Heron's formula with a = 11, b = 9.0, c = 8.0 gives S = 14 and Δ = √1260 ≈ 35.50 square units.
  • Large SAS case: b = 414, c = 485, α = 49°47′ gives Δ = 100395 × sin49°47′ ≈ 76662.45 square units.
  • A triangular garden with a 30 m side and corner angles 22(1)/(2)° and 112(1)/(2)° has area 225 m², costing Rs. 1125 at Rs. 5 per m².
  • A back yard with sides 53 ft and 42 ft and included angle 135° has area (1)/(2) × 53 × 42 × sin135° ≈ 787 square feet.

Solved Exercises

Q: Q1(i). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 15, b = 80, γ = 38°

Ans: Formula used (area, SAS case): Δ = (1)/(2) ab sin γ.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has sides a = BC = 15 and b = CA = 80 with the included angle γ = 38° at C between them. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: Δ = (1)/(2) × 15 × 80 × sin38°
Step 2: Δ = 600 × 0.61566 ≈ 369.40
Answer: Δ ≈ 369.40 square units

Q: Q1(ii). Find the area of ΔABC: b = 14, c = 12, α = 82°

Ans: Formula used (area, SAS case): Δ = (1)/(2) bc sin α.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has sides b = CA = 14 and c = AB = 12 with the included angle α = 82° at A between them. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: Δ = (1)/(2) × 14 × 12 × sin82°
Step 2: Δ = 84 × 0.99027 ≈ 83.18
Answer: Δ ≈ 83.18 square units

Q: Q1(iii). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 30, β = 50°, γ = 100°

Ans: Formula used (area, SAA case): Δ = (1)/(2) a² (sin β sin γ)/(sin α), after finding α from the angle sum.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has side a = BC = 30 opposite α, with angles β = 50° at B and γ = 100° at C given. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: α = 180° − β − γ = 180° − 50° − 100° = 30°
Step 2: Δ = (1)/(2) × 30² × (sin50° × sin100°)/(sin30°)
Step 3: Δ = 450 × (0.76604 × 0.98481)/(0.5) = 450 × 0.75441/(0.5) ≈ 678.97
Answer: Δ ≈ 678.97 square units (the book's key gives 680, a rounded value)

Q: Q1(iv). Find the area of ΔABC: b = 40, α = 50°, γ = 60°

Ans: Formula used (area, SAA case): Δ = (1)/(2) b² (sin α sin γ)/(sin β), after finding β from the angle sum.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has side b = CA = 40 opposite β, with angles α = 50° at A and γ = 60° at C given. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: β = 180° − α − γ = 180° − 50° − 60° = 70°
Step 2: Δ = (1)/(2) × 40² × (sin50° × sin60°)/(sin70°)
Step 3: Δ = 800 × (0.76604 × 0.86603)/(0.93969) = 800 × 0.66341/(0.93969) ≈ 564.79
Answer: Δ ≈ 564.79 square units

Q: Q1(v). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 7.0, b = 8.0, c = 2.0

Ans: Formula used (area, SSS case): Heron's formula Δ = √(S(S − a)(S − b)(S − c)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has all three sides known: a = BC = 7.0, b = CA = 8.0 and c = AB = 2.0. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(7.0 + 8.0 + 2.0) = (17)/(2) = 8.5
Step 2: S − a = 1.5, S − b = 0.5, S − c = 6.5
Step 3: Δ = √(8.5 × 1.5 × 0.5 × 6.5) = √41.4375 ≈ 6.44
Answer: Δ ≈ 6.44 square units

Q: Q1(vi). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 11, b = 9.0, c = 8.0

Ans: Formula used (area, SSS case): Heron's formula Δ = √(S(S − a)(S − b)(S − c)), where S = (1)/(2)(a + b + c).
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has all three sides known: a = BC = 11, b = CA = 9.0 and c = AB = 8.0. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: S = (1)/(2)(11 + 9 + 8) = (28)/(2) = 14
Step 2: S − a = 3, S − b = 5, S − c = 6
Step 3: Δ = √(14 × 3 × 5 × 6) = √1260 ≈ 35.50
Answer: Δ ≈ 35.50 square units

Q: Q1(vii). Find the area of ΔABC: b = 414, c = 485, α = 49°47′

Ans: Formula used (area, SAS case): Δ = (1)/(2) bc sin α.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has sides b = CA = 414 and c = AB = 485 with the included angle α = 49°47′ at A between them. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: Δ = (1)/(2) × 414 × 485 × sin49°47′
Step 2: Δ = 100395 × 0.76361 ≈ 76662.45
Answer: Δ ≈ 76662.45 square units

Q: Q1(viii). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 32, β = 47°24′, γ = 70°16′

Ans: Formula used (area, SAA case): Δ = (1)/(2) a² (sin β sin γ)/(sin α), after finding α from the angle sum.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has side a = BC = 32 opposite α, with angles β = 47°24′ at B and γ = 70°16′ at C given. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: α = 180° − 47°24′ − 70°16′ = 62°20′
Step 2: Δ = (1)/(2) × 32² × (sin47°24′ × sin70°16′)/(sin62°20′)
Step 3: Δ = 512 × (0.73609 × 0.94140)/(0.88539) = 512 × 0.69296/(0.88539) ≈ 400.55
Answer: Δ ≈ 400.55 square units

Q: Q1(ix). Find the area of ΔABC: b = 47, α = 60°25′, γ = 41°35′

Ans: Formula used (area, SAA case): Δ = (1)/(2) b² (sin α sin γ)/(sin β), after finding β from the angle sum.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has side b = CA = 47 opposite β, with angles α = 60°25′ at A and γ = 41°35′ at C given. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: β = 180° − 60°25′ − 41°35′ = 78°00′
Step 2: Δ = (1)/(2) × 47² × (sin60°25′ × sin41°35′)/(sin78°00′)
Step 3: Δ = 1104.5 × (0.86976 × 0.66344)/(0.97815) = 1104.5 × 0.57707/(0.97815) ≈ 651.74
Answer: Δ ≈ 651.74 square units

Q: Q1(x). Find the area of ΔABC: c = 57, α = 23°24′, β = 71°36′

Ans: Formula used (area, SAA case): Δ = (1)/(2) c² (sin α sin β)/(sin γ), after finding γ from the angle sum.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has side c = AB = 57 opposite γ, with angles α = 23°24′ at A and β = 71°36′ at B given. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: γ = 180° − 23°24′ − 71°36′ = 85°00′
Step 2: Δ = (1)/(2) × 57² × (sin23°24′ × sin71°36′)/(sin85°00′)
Step 3: Δ = 1624.5 × (0.39715 × 0.94888)/(0.99619) = 1624.5 × 0.37685/(0.99619) ≈ 614.52
Answer: Δ ≈ 614.52 square units

Q: Q1(xi). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 925, c = 433, β = 42°17′

Ans: Formula used (area, SAS case): Δ = (1)/(2) ac sin β.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has sides a = BC = 925 and c = AB = 433 with the included angle β = 42°17′ at B between them. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: Δ = (1)/(2) × 925 × 433 × sin42°17′
Step 2: Δ = 200262.5 × 0.67280 ≈ 134736.08
Answer: Δ ≈ 134736.08 square units

Q: Q1(xii). Find the area of ΔABC: a = 92, b = 71, γ = 56°44′

Ans: Formula used (area, SAS case): Δ = (1)/(2) ab sin γ.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has sides a = BC = 92 and b = CA = 71 with the included angle γ = 56°44′ at C between them. The area Δ of the triangle is to be found.
Step 1: Δ = (1)/(2) × 92 × 71 × sin56°44′
Step 2: Δ = 3266 × 0.83581 ≈ 2730.79
Answer: Δ ≈ 2730.79 square units

Q: Q2. The area of a triangle is 121.34. If α = 32°25′, β = 65°65′, then find c and angle γ.

Ans: Formula used: γ = 180° − α − β, and the area formula Δ = (1)/(2) c² (sin α sin β)/(sin γ), solved for c.
Diagram (in words): ΔABC has area 121.34 square units, with angles α = 32°25′ at A and β at B, and side c = AB opposite γ. As printed, β = 65°65′; since 65′ = 1°05′, this is read as β = 66°05′. We have to find side c and the angle γ at C.
Step 1: β = 65°65′ = 65° + 65′ = 65° + 1°05′ = 66°05′
Step 2: γ = 180° − α − β = 180° − 32°25′ − 66°05′ = 81°30′
Step 3: from Δ = (1)/(2) c² (sin α sin β)/(sin γ), we get c² = (2Δ sin γ)/(sin α sin β)
Step 4: c² = (2 × 121.34 × sin81°30′)/(sin32°25′ × sin66°05′) = (242.68 × 0.98877)/(0.53644 × 0.91474) = (239.96)/(0.49071) ≈ 489.02
Step 5: c = √489.02 ≈ 22.13
Answer: γ = 81°30′, c ≈ 22.13
Note: The angle β is misprinted in the book as 65°65′ (minutes cannot exceed 59); it is read above as 66°05′. The book's printed answers (c = 22.24, γ = 82°8′) do not agree with any consistent reading of the printed data.

Q: Q3. One side of a triangular garden is 30 m. If its two corner angles are 22(1)/(2)° and 112(1)/(2)°, find the cost of planting the grass at the rate of Rs. 5 per square meter.

Ans: Formula used: the area formula Δ = (1)/(2) c² (sin α sin β)/(sin γ) for a side with its two adjacent angles, then cost = area × rate.
Diagram (in words): The triangular garden has one side of 30 m whose two end (corner) angles are 22(1)/(2)° and 112(1)/(2)°. The third corner angle is 180° − 22(1)/(2)° − 112(1)/(2)° = 45°. The 30 m side is opposite the 45° angle. We have to find the area of the garden and then the cost of grass at Rs. 5 per square metre.
Step 1: third angle γ = 180° − 22.5° − 112.5° = 45°
Step 2: Δ = (1)/(2) × 30² × (sin22.5° × sin112.5°)/(sin45°)
Step 3: Δ = 450 × (0.38268 × 0.92388)/(0.70711) = 450 × (0.35355)/(0.70711) = 450 × 0.5 = 225 m²
Step 4: cost = 225 × 5 = Rs. 1125
Answer: The cost of planting the grass is Rs. 1125

Q: Q4. A new home owner has a triangular-shaped back yard. Two of the three sides measure 53 ft and 42 ft and form an included angle of 135°. Find the area of the back yard (to the nearest square foot).

Ans: Formula used (area, SAS case): Δ = (1)/(2) × (product of the two sides) × sin(included angle).
Diagram (in words): The back yard is a triangle with two sides of 53 ft and 42 ft meeting at a vertex with the included angle 135° between them. The area of the yard is to be found.
Step 1: Δ = (1)/(2) × 53 × 42 × sin135°
Step 2: Δ = 1113 × 0.70711 ≈ 787.01
Answer: The area of the back yard is ≈ 787 square feet
